findings.summary: A phone hitting an unmatched marketing path never reaches the new 404: the mobile-UA proxy rewrites it to the Expo mobile-web build, which answers HTTP 200 with its own black "Unmatched Route" screen.
findings.detail: Flow "404 /nope", mobile 375x812 (iPhone 13 device profile), status failed. Evidence: apps/web/test-output/artifacts/rv-10-404-mobile.png shows a black page reading "Unmatched Route" / "Page could not be found." / "Go back • Sitemap" with the URL printed on it, and rv-evidence-summary.json records `10-404__mobile: { status: 200, h1: "Unmatched Route", styleFacts: { wrapperClass: null, buttonBg: null, eyebrowHasDotSpan: false } }` against `10-404__desktop: { status: 404, h1: "Let’s get you back on track." }`. The driver reproduced it a second way with a raw curl under an iPhone UA returning the Expo web shell. I confirmed the mechanism in source: MARKETING_PATHS is an exact-match Set (middleware.ts:28-37), so isMarketingPath("/nope") is false, skipMobileRedirect is false (middleware.ts:73-78) and the request is unconditionally rewritten to MOBILE_WEB_URL (middleware.ts:88) before Next's not-found handling runs. Two things keep this from being a blocker on this change: (1) it is PRE-EXISTING and deliberately preserved — spec R11 says the rewrite skips the nine marketing paths and "every other path keeps today's behaviour byte-for-byte", and test-plan T11 records that on the untouched tree every path rewrites for a mobile UA; (2) no acceptance criterion covers it — T1's bogus-path 404 assertion runs in the desktop `marketing` project, and the mobile T2/T12 rows do not test an unmatched path. The user-facing cost is real though: a phone visitor following a stale or typo'd link to the marketing domain gets an unbranded Expo screen instead of the 404 this change just built, and it answers 200, which is a soft-404 for crawlers. Consequence for coverage: because this flow diverted, the new marketing 404 was never observed at the 375px viewport in this run — its styling is verified at desktop only.
findings.fixHint: Owner/spec decision, not a mechanical fix: either widen the mobile carve-out to cover unmatched paths (e.g. let the mobile proxy handle only paths the mobile build actually has routes for, or exclude anything that is not a known app route) or explicitly accept the pre-port behaviour and record it as a residual in spec R11. middleware.ts is HIGH-risk — the same block gates the signed-in "/" redirect contract (CC-11…CC-15) — so any change needs the T11 pins re-run plus a rendered re-check of /nope under a mobile UA and of the marketing 404 at 375px.

finalPass.decision:
All three reader candidates are real and none duplicates the already-raised list. #0 (major) is the missing half of the middleware story: the run already caught phones WITH presence cookies being 307'd to non-existent mobile routes, but not phones WITHOUT them — every existing mobile-web user now lands on the marketing page at `/` because the Expo build never writes the cookies the guard reads; this needs a product ruling (intended landing vs. regression) and a middleware fix either way. #1 (major) is the consequence of exempting page paths only: the marketing head's same-origin icons, manifest and OG image are still rewritten to the mobile-web origin for phone UAs, so the middleware carve-out must cover the layout's asset paths (or the matcher must exclude /brand/ and the metadata routes). #2 is held at blocker because it matches Next 14's documented standalone-without-sharp failure and would blank the brand mark on every auth, admin and preview surface the diff touched; it is unproven only because the UI checks ran against dev — the fixer must build the production web image and request /_next/image before this ships, and if it reproduces, the fix is either an `unoptimized` BrandMark or adding sharp to apps/web and its Dockerfile. Two further reads are warranted (next.config + Dockerfile runner; the phone sign-in path from the marketing header through MARKETING_PATHS and the Expo auth storage); beyond those the read was sufficient.
Second read: All five candidates stand. The strongest new theme is that exempting "/" from the mobile-UA proxy makes phones render the Next marketing site for the first time while everything that site links or references — the /signup and buyer auth CTAs (#0), the /brand icons and manifest (#2) — is still proxied to the Expo mobile-web origin, which answers with its own SPA HTML or landing screen; the signed-in guard meant to soften that transition is dead because Expo never writes the presence cookies (#1). Separately, the first next/image use in an output: standalone app with no images config and no sharp in the web workspace (#3) is a plausible prod-wide 500 for every BrandMark that the fixer must settle against the actual Dockerfile install and trace before touching code — a one-line unoptimized setting closes it either way. The duplicate Geist assets (#4) are a minor hygiene item. Severities: #0 major, #1 minor, #2 major, #3 major, #4 minor; no further gaps — the run ends here.

findings.summary: The `signedIn` guard that keeps phones out of the marketing landing page reads presence cookies that only the Next web app writes — the mobile-web build never sets them — so every existing phone user of the mobile app now lands on the public marketing page at `/` instead of their app.
findings.detail:
State path: an operator uses RouteFlow on their phone at `https://www.routeflow.info`. Today (pre-diff) `skipMobileRedirect = optedOutOfMobile || /api/ || /_next/`, so EVERY phone request to `/` is rewritten to `MOBILE_WEB_URL/` and they land in the Expo mobile-web build, which does its own role routing. They sign in there; the middleware comment (middleware.ts:17-19) confirms the address bar stays on www.routeflow.info, so this is where these users live.

After the diff, middleware.ts:73-77 makes `/` exempt from the proxy unless `signedIn` (line 67) is true, and `signedIn` is read from `rf-op-auth` / `rf-buyer-auth`. Evidence those cookies cannot exist for a mobile-web user: `apps/web/lib/presence-cookies.ts:26-50` sets them with `document.cookie` from inside the Next web app only (callers: `apps/web/lib/auth.ts:7`, `apps/web/lib/buyer-auth.ts:95`); a grep for `rf-op-auth|rf-buyer-auth|OP_PRESENCE_COOKIE|BUYER_PRESENCE_COOKIE` and for `document.cookie` across `apps/mobile/**/*.ts(x)` returns ZERO hits. The Expo build keeps its session in its own storage.

So for the entire existing mobile population `signedIn === false` and `/` is exempt. Concretely: a signed-in mobile-web operator opens their bookmark `https://www.routeflow.info/` → no presence cookie → line 77 is true → no rewrite → `resolveLandingTarget` returns null → they are served the desktop marketing landing page with 'Book a demo', not their app. The escape route makes it worse, not better: tapping 'Sign in → Distributor' goes to `/login`, which is NOT in MARKETING_PATHS, so it IS proxied — they bounce into the mobile app's login screen despite already being signed in there.

The new test file pins exactly this behaviour as correct: `does not proxy / for a signed-out phone (R-MKT T11)` passes (I ran `npx jest --runInBand middleware.marketing` in apps/web: 25/25 pass). Nothing in the suite models a phone whose session lives in the mobile-web build, because that session is invisible to the middleware by construction.

This is the opposite failure from the already-known '/ redirect fires on phones and sends them to /dashboard' item: the implementation's `signedIn` clause does prevent that, but the signal it depends on is unobtainable for the users it was written to protect, so the clause is effectively dead for them. (It can only ever fire for a phone that signed in through the desktop UI after `?desktop=1` AND whose 30-day `prefer-desktop` cookie has since lapsed while the sliding presence cookie stayed fresh.)
findings.fixHint: Decide the intended contract for `/` on a phone. Options: (a) keep proxying `/` for phones unconditionally (drop `/` from the carve-out) and reach the marketing home on phones via an explicit path/`?desktop=1`; (b) have the mobile-web build set the presence cookie on sign-in so the middleware can see it; (c) serve the marketing landing at `/` on phones but give the mobile-web build a visible re-entry link. Any choice needs a middleware test that models a phone with NO presence cookie but an active mobile-web session.
findings.decision: The presence cookies are written only by the Next web app's document.cookie callers, so a mobile-web user who was signed in inside the Expo build carries no rf-op-auth/rf-buyer-auth and, with `/` now exempt from the proxy, is served the marketing landing instead of their app on every visit to the root. This is the complement of the already-raised 'signed-in phone redirect' finding (cookies present) and is not covered by it; it is an undecided behavior change for every existing phone user's entry path, not a deliberate product ruling.

findings.summary: MARKETING_PATHS enrolls page paths only; every same-origin non-`_next` subresource the marketing HTML asks for (icons, apple-touch-icon, the web app manifest, the OG image, /sw.js) is still rewritten to the mobile-web origin for phone user agents.
findings.detail:
The carve-out is exact-path over `MARKETING_PAGE_PATHS` + `/robots.txt` + `/sitemap.xml` (middleware.ts:29-33). The matcher is `"/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)"` (middleware.ts, `config` at EOF), so every OTHER same-origin path still reaches the mobile-UA rewrite at middleware.ts:79-90. I confirmed the mechanism by running the new suite: the pin `still rewrites /product/anything for a mobile UA (MKT-PIN T11)` passes, i.e. any non-exempt path with an iPhone UA becomes `NextResponse.rewrite(https://routeflowmobile-production.up.railway.app<path>)`.

The marketing pages are now, for the first time, rendered on phones — and the `<head>` the root layout emits (apps/web/app/layout.tsx) asks the same origin for: `/brand/routeflow-mark-64.png` (icons.icon + shortcut, layout.tsx:85,87), `/brand/routeflow-mark-180.png` (icons.apple, :86), `/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png` (appleWebApp.startupImage, :82), `/operator-manifest.json` (manifest, :77) and `/brand/routeflow-mark-512.png` (openGraph.images, :94). `ServiceWorkerRegistry` (layout.tsx:110, components/ServiceWorkerRegistry.tsx:7) additionally requests `/sw.js`. None of these six paths is in MARKETING_PATHS and none matches the matcher's exclusions, so on a phone each is proxied to the Expo Railway origin, which does not serve them.

Observable failures for a phone visitor on /, /product, /pricing, …: no apple-touch-icon; the manifest response is the Expo build's HTML, so Chrome logs `Manifest: Line: 1, column: 1, Syntax error` and 'Add to Home Screen' is unavailable from the new marketing site; `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js')` rejects on an unsupported MIME type (swallowed by the .catch, so it is a console error only); and Googlebot-Smartphone (UA contains both `Android` and `Mobile`, so `isMobileUserAgent` matches) cannot fetch the og:image it is told about.

Why every earlier lens missed it: the unit suite only iterates `MARKETING_PAGE_PATHS` plus the two metadata routes; the UI-verify `console-errors` / `network-failures` flows ran a desktop browser resized to 375px, which sends a DESKTOP user agent, so the proxy never engaged; Playwright T12 asserts only the /pricing HTML body. Note this is NOT the known '/unmatched marketing path never reaches the 404' item — that is about page routes; this is about the subresources a successfully-served marketing page then requests. The visible marks are fine, because BrandMark goes through `next/image` → `/_next/image?...`, which the matcher does exclude.
findings.fixHint: Extend the proxy skip beyond exact page paths — e.g. also skip `/brand/`, `/marketing/`, `/sw.js` and the two manifest JSONs, or (cleaner) exclude static asset paths in the middleware `matcher` itself the way `_next/static` already is. Add a middleware test row asserting `/brand/routeflow-mark-64.png` and `/operator-manifest.json` are NOT rewritten for a mobile UA.
findings.decision: The exemption is exact-match over page paths plus robots/sitemap while the matcher excludes only _next/static, _next/image and favicon.ico, and the passing T11 pin proves any other path with a phone UA is rewritten to the mobile-web origin — so the root layout's /brand/*.png icons, apple-touch icon, manifest and OG image requested by a phone rendering the marketing HTML are fetched from the wrong origin. Pre-diff this was invisible because the whole phone session was proxied consistently; now the page and its head assets split origins.

findings.summary: This diff introduces `next/image` into apps/web for the first time (and puts it on the login, signup, all buyer auth, platform-admin and two money-preview surfaces), but apps/web declares no `sharp` dependency and the web runner image is a bare standalone bundle — if sharp is not traced in, `/_next/image` 500s and the brand mark vanishes app-wide.
findings.detail:
Evidence gathered this session: (1) `grep -rln "from \"next/image\"" apps/web/app apps/web/components packages/ui/src` excluding `(marketing)` returns exactly one file — `apps/web/components/brand/BrandMark.tsx:1`. Inside `(marketing)` it returns company/page.tsx, components/operation-story.tsx, components/technology-art.tsx. So before this diff apps/web used `next/image` nowhere; after it, every BrandMark render on `(auth)/login`, `(auth)/signup`, the eight `buyer/*` pages, `(platform-admin)/layout.tsx`, `(dashboard)/customers/[id]` statement preview and `(dashboard)/bookkeeping/[transactionId]` invoice preview goes through the image optimizer. (2) `grep '"sharp"' apps/web/package.json` → no match; in package-lock.json the only owner of `node_modules/sharp` (0.35.4) is `apps/api`. (3) `apps/web/Dockerfile` builder copies root manifests + `packages/*` + `apps/web/package.json` only — `apps/api/package.json` is never copied — then `npm ci`; the runner stage is `node:20-alpine` with only `.next/standalone`, `.next/static` and `public` copied in. (4) `next.config.mjs` sets `output: "standalone"` and does NOT set `images: { unoptimized: true }`. Next is pinned at 14.2.35 (apps/web/package.json:44).

Failure scenario if sharp is not resolvable in the deployed standalone server: every `/_next/image?url=%2Fbrand%2Froutefow-mark-192.png…` request answers 500, so the shared mark is a broken image on every authenticated and auth-entry surface the port just converted to it, and the marketing photography fails too — i.e. the visible half of R4/R12 is dead on deploy day while every Jest/tsc/eslint gate stays green (RTL never renders the optimizer).

HONEST LIMIT: I did NOT verify the outcome. Proving it needs a `docker build -f apps/web/Dockerfile` and an inspection of `.next/standalone/node_modules/sharp`, which I did not run. What I verified is the exposure: a first-time `next/image` dependency in a standalone image whose workspace does not declare sharp and whose only lockfile owner of sharp is a workspace the web build does not even copy the manifest for. The musl binary (`@img/sharp-linuxmusl-x64`) IS in the lockfile and apps/api runs alpine, so sharp is installable — the open question is purely whether it is present and traced into the web standalone output.
findings.fixHint: Either add `sharp` to apps/web's dependencies (belt-and-braces for standalone, as Next documents), or prove with one Docker build that `.next/standalone/**/sharp` exists and `/_next/image` returns 200 for `/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png` before this ships. If neither is acceptable, drop back to plain `` for BrandMark (it is a fixed-size square PNG, so optimization buys little) and keep `next/image` only where R12 requires it.
findings.decision: apps/web declares no sharp, package-lock puts it only under apps/api, and the web runner is a standalone bundle — exactly the configuration in which Next 14 refuses /_next/image at request time ('sharp is required to be installed in standalone mode'), which would blank the BrandMark on login, signup, every buyer auth page, platform-admin and the two money previews. The evidence does not show images.unoptimized or an `unoptimized` prop that would neutralise it, and the visual checks ran against dev, not the Docker image, so the candidate stays; it is the one item that must be proved against the production image before merge.

findings.summary: Three of the four auth CTAs the new marketing chrome ships (/signup, /buyer/login, /buyer/register) are not in the mobile-proxy exemption set, so on a phone they are rewritten to the Expo mobile-web build, which has no such routes — the visitor is silently dumped on the Expo app's own landing screen and never reaches a sign-up or retailer sign-in form.
findings.detail:
State path, verified end to end in this session:

(1) The exemption set is exactly `MARKETING_PAGE_PATHS` + two metadata routes. `apps/web/lib/marketing-routes.ts:19-30` lists `/`, `/product`, `/wholesalers`, `/retailers`, `/pricing`, `/company`, `/contact`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/distributors`. `middleware.ts:29-33` spreads that plus `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`. `/login`, `/signup`, `/buyer/login`, `/buyer/register` are NOT members, so `middleware.ts:77` leaves `skipMobileRedirect` false and `middleware.ts:79-88` rewrites to `https://routeflowmobile-production.up.railway.app<pathname>`.

(2) The new chrome links all four on every page. `app/(marketing)/components/auth-links.ts:7-10` = `/login`, `/signup`, `/buyer/login`, `/buyer/register`. `site-footer.tsx:42-50` renders all four in the 'Your workspace' column of the footer, i.e. on all 9 public pages. `site-header.tsx:80-93` (sign-in dropdown) and `:140-147` (mobile sheet) render `/login` + `/buyer/login`. `retailers/page.tsx:64` is the page's primary green CTA -> `authLinks.retailerSignUp` (`/buyer/register`), `:71` -> `/buyer/login`.

(3) The Expo build has none of those routes. `find apps/mobile/app -maxdepth 2 -type d` returns only `(auth)`, `(customer)`, `(driver)`, `(operator)`, `(tenant)`; `ls apps/mobile/app/(auth)` shows `login.tsx` but no `signup`; there is no `buyer` segment anywhere in the tree, and `find apps/mobile/app -name '+not-found*'` returns nothing.

(4) The mobile service answers 200 for any path: `apps/mobile/Dockerfile` nginx block `location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; }`.

(5) What the visitor then sees: expo-router registers its built-in `Unmatched` screen for `NOT_FOUND_ROUTE_NAME` (`apps/mobile/node_modules/expo-router/build/ExpoRoot.js:153`; `constants.js:5` -> `'+not-found'`; `views/Unmatched.js:54-56` renders an h1 'Unmatched Route'). Then `apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:88-104` fires: for a signed-out visitor, `segments[0]` is `'+not-found'`, which is neither `(auth)` nor `(customer)`/`(operator)`/`(driver)`, so it hits the else branch `router.replace("/")` and the browser lands on the Expo app's static landing screen (`apps/mobile/app/index.tsx`, a marketing screen, not a router).

Concrete failure: a retailer on an iPhone opens www.routeflow.info/retailers, taps the page's main green 'Create retailer account' button -> the URL becomes /buyer/register, the Expo SPA boots, flashes 'Unmatched Route', then client-side replaces the URL with '/' and shows the Expo mobile landing page. The registration form is unreachable on a phone. Same for footer 'Create distributor account' (/signup) and 'Retailer sign in' (/buyer/login) on all 9 pages. Only /login survives (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx exists, and `_layout.tsx:88` skips the replace because `segments[0] === "(auth)"`).

Why nothing caught it: T3 (`e2e/36-marketing-site.spec.ts:246-290`) crawls the links with the `marketing` project's context, which `playwright.config.ts:565-568` pins to `devices["Desktop Chrome"]` — desktop UA, so the Next pages answer normally. Even a UA-swapped rerun would pass, because the nginx fallback returns 200 for every one of these paths; the assertion is on `status < 400`, not on content. This directly contradicts R3 ('Every internal link resolves on the live app') for the population R11 was written to serve.
findings.fixHint: Decide the contract for phones: either add the four auth paths to the mobile-proxy exemption (so phones get the Next auth pages, matching the desktop marketing site they came from), or point the marketing chrome's auth links at the mobile-web equivalents when the visitor is on a phone. Then add a mobile-UA content assertion (not a status assertion) to T3.
findings.decision: The evidence traces the full path: the exemption set is exactly MARKETING_PAGE_PATHS plus two metadata routes, the new chrome links /signup, /buyer/login and /buyer/register from every page's footer and header, and a phone UA on those paths is rewritten to the Expo mobile-web origin which has no such routes. Rendering the marketing site on phones for the first time turns its primary conversion CTAs into dead ends, a regression the port itself creates; /login still reaches an Expo login screen, so major rather than blocker.

findings.summary: The `!(pathname === "/" && signedIn)` guard that is supposed to preserve the pre-port landing behaviour for signed-in phones can never fire, because the Expo mobile-web build never writes the presence cookies it reads — so returning mobile-web users lose their 'type the domain, land in my app' entry point.
findings.detail:
`middleware.ts:70-77` computes `signedIn` from `OP_PRESENCE_COOKIE` / `BUYER_PRESENCE_COOKIE` and uses it to keep the pre-port proxy for a signed-in phone at '/'. The comment at `middleware.ts:64-69` and again at `:89-96` states 'a signed-in phone at "/" was already proxied to the mobile-web build and never reaches this block'.

That is false in production. The presence cookies are written only by `apps/web/lib/presence-cookies.ts:27-29` via `document.cookie`, from the Next.js web app's auth code. `grep -rni cookie` over `apps/mobile/{app,lib,hooks,store,utils,components}` (ts/tsx, node_modules excluded) returns ZERO hits — the Expo build stores its session in AsyncStorage/SecureStore and never touches `document.cookie`. So for every mobile-web user `signedIn === false`, `isMarketingPath("/")` is true, and '/' is exempted from the proxy.

What changes for them: `apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:71-80` routes a signed-in buyer at '/' to `/(customer)/(tabs)/home`, and `:167-172` routes a signed-in operator at '/' to `/(operator)/home`. So before this change, a returning mobile-web user who opened www.routeflow.info was auto-routed into their app. After it, they get the desktop marketing homepage instead, and their only way back is to tap a control labelled 'Sign in' (`/login`, which does proxy through and, via `_layout.tsx:167`, lands them in the app) — while the two retailer controls are the dead ends of the finding above.

Second consequence: the test block 'middleware landing carve-out, signed in' in `apps/web/app/(marketing)/middleware.marketing.test.ts` manufactures `rf-op-auth=1` / `rf-buyer-auth=1` on an iPhone request. Those two rows are green and vacuous — they pin a state the mobile build cannot produce, so they give false assurance that the pre-port landing behaviour is preserved for phones.
findings.fixHint: Either accept and document that mobile-web users now see the marketing homepage (and drop or re-scope the dead `signedIn` clause plus its two vacuous test rows), or give the mobile-web build a way to advertise its session to the middleware (it runs on the same www.routeflow.info origin for the document, so a presence cookie written by the Expo web bootstrap would work).
findings.decision: The presence cookies are written only by apps/web's presence-cookies.ts and a grep of the Expo app shows it never touches document.cookie, so signedIn is always false for a mobile-web user and the guard plus its two comments describe behaviour that cannot occur. The user-facing cost is one extra tap (Sign in → /login → Expo), but the code carries a false correctness claim and dead logic that will mislead the next editor.

findings.summary: Every marketing page now renders on phones declaring a manifest, favicon, apple-touch-icon and OG image under /brand and /operator-manifest.json — none of which are in the mobile-proxy exemption, so a phone gets the Expo SPA's index.html (200, text/html) for all of them.
findings.detail:
The middleware matcher is `["/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)"]` (`middleware.ts:226`) — it excludes only `_next/static`, `_next/image` and `/favicon.ico`. `/brand/*` and `/operator-manifest.json` therefore reach the middleware, are not members of `MARKETING_PATHS` (`middleware.ts:29-33`), and under a mobile UA are rewritten to the mobile-web origin, where nginx's `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html` (`apps/mobile/Dockerfile`) returns the Expo SPA HTML with a 200.

The root layout now points every one of these at those paths: `app/layout.tsx:77` `manifest: "/operator-manifest.json"`, `:82` `startupImage: "/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png"`, `:85` `icon: /brand/routeflow-mark-64.png`, `:86` `apple: /brand/routeflow-mark-180.png`, `:87` `shortcut: /brand/routeflow-mark-64.png`, `:94` `openGraph.images: /brand/routeflow-mark-512.png`.

This is new because before the port a phone never rendered any of this HTML — every public path was proxied at the door. Concrete failures on an iPhone at www.routeflow.info/pricing: the `<link rel="manifest">` fetch returns HTML, so the manifest fails to parse and 'Add to Home Screen' has no name/icons/start_url; the apple-touch-icon fetch returns HTML, so the home-screen icon falls back to a screenshot; the tab/favicon fetch returns HTML. Googlebot-Smartphone (UA contains both 'Android' and 'Mobile', so `isMobileUserAgent` at `middleware.ts:36-42` matches it — the new test file's own comment says so) gets HTML for the og:image URL.

Not affected, and worth noting so the fix is scoped correctly: `BrandMark` and the three marketing photos go through `next/image`, whose browser request is `/_next/image?url=...`, and `_next/image` IS excluded by the matcher, so those render.
findings.fixHint: Add the static asset prefixes the public pages reference (`/brand/`, `/marketing/`) and the two manifest JSON files to the mobile-proxy skip list, or exclude them in the middleware matcher alongside `_next/static`.
findings.decision: The matcher excludes only _next/static, _next/image and /favicon.ico, /brand/* and /operator-manifest.json are not in MARKETING_PATHS, and nginx's try_files on the mobile-web origin answers 200 text/html for unknown paths — so every phone visitor to the marketing site gets SPA HTML for the manifest, icons, apple-touch-icon and startup image the new root layout declares. This is new exposure because before the port a phone never rendered a Next page that referenced these assets.

findings.summary: This change introduces the app's first-ever use of next/image while apps/web has no `images` config (so optimization is on) and `output: "standalone"` — a combination in which Next 14.2.35 hard-throws a 500 if `sharp` is missing, and `sharp` is not a dependency of the web workspace nor of the web Docker build's manifest set.
findings.detail:
Verified facts:

- `apps/web/next.config.mjs` has NO `images` key at all — no `unoptimized: true`, no loader override — so `<Image>` uses the default loader and the browser requests `/_next/image?url=...`. Line 9 of that file sets `output: "standalone"`.
- `node_modules/next/dist/server/image-optimizer.js:664-668`: in `optimizeImage`, when `sharp` is falsy AND `nextConfigOutput === "standalone"`, Next logs `'sharp' is required to be installed in standalone mode...` and `throw new ImageError(500, "Internal Server Error")`. The squoosh fallback below it is unreachable in standalone. `sharp` is loaded at `:155-157` via `require(process.env.NEXT_SHARP_PATH || "sharp")` inside a try/catch, so a missing module leaves it undefined silently.
- `sharp` is not in `apps/web/package.json`. The only manifest declaring it is `apps/api/package.json:84`.
- `apps/web/Dockerfile` builder copies root `package.json`/`package-lock.json`/`turbo.json`, the `packages/*` manifests, and `apps/web/package.json` — it never copies `apps/api/package.json` (contrast `apps/api/Dockerfile:27`, which copies its own). So apps/api is not an on-disk workspace in the web image.
- `git grep next/image HEAD -- apps/web` returns only a middleware matcher string and two eslint-disable comments — no component ever imported `next/image` before this change. There is therefore zero production evidence that `/_next/image` works in the deployed web image.

NOT verified, and I am saying so explicitly: I could not confirm whether root `npm ci` still materialises `node_modules/sharp` from the lockfile when apps/api is absent, nor whether @vercel/nft traces the dynamic `require(process.env.NEXT_SHARP_PATH || "sharp")` into `.next/standalone`. `next build` was never run in this worktree (only a dev `.next`; `apps/web/.next/standalone` does not exist), and I did not build the image. `node_modules/next/dist/build/collect-build-traces.js:250-254` only *ignores* sharp under `hasNextSupport` (Vercel), so it is not deliberately excluded — but nothing in the repo pins it in either.

Failure scenario if sharp is absent from the runner: every `/_next/image` request returns 500. `BrandMark` renders nothing on the operator login page, signup, buyer login/register/invite/change-password/forgot/reset/verify, the buyer-portal sidebar, the customer statement preview, the bookkeeping invoice preview and the platform-admin sidebar; and the three `next/image` photos (`(marketing)/company/page.tsx:2`, `components/operation-story.tsx:4`, `components/technology-art.tsx:1`) fail on the marketing pages. Because `alt=""` on the mark, it degrades to blank space rather than a broken-image glyph — silent on every surface.
findings.fixHint: Pin it rather than leave it to tracing luck: either add `sharp` to apps/web's dependencies (and confirm the alpine musl binaries land, as apps/api already does), or set `images: { unoptimized: true }` in next.config.mjs since every image here is a local static asset. Whichever is chosen, prove it against a built image before merge — this is the first next/image in the app.
findings.decision: The quoted image-optimizer.js lines show Next 14.2 hard-throws a 500 when sharp is absent under output: "standalone" in production, next.config.mjs has no images config so optimization is on, and sharp is declared only by apps/api. Whether hoisting plus standalone tracing happens to carry apps/api's sharp into the web runner image is not settled by the truncated Dockerfile evidence, so this is kept: if it does not, every BrandMark on every page is a 500 in prod and the fix (unoptimized) is one line.

findings.summary: The port adds a second copy of the Geist typeface to git (141 KB of woff2 under apps/web/fonts/) while an unreferenced 134 KB woff copy of the same family already sits tracked at apps/web/app/fonts/, and the spec's residual row naming the heavy-files exemption omits the new fonts directory.
findings.detail:
`apps/web/app/fonts.ts:8,16` points `next/font/local` at `../fonts/Geist-Variable.woff2` and `../fonts/GeistMono-Variable.woff2` — new untracked binaries (69,652 B and 71,368 B, `ls -la apps/web/fonts`).

`git ls-files apps/web/app/fonts` shows `app/fonts/GeistVF.woff` and `app/fonts/GeistMonoVF.woff` are already tracked (66,268 B + 67,864 B, dated 2026-09-04, i.e. pre-existing on HEAD). `grep -rn "GeistVF\|GeistMonoVF"` across apps/web (ts/tsx/css/js, node_modules and .next excluded) returns nothing — they are referenced by no code, no CSS and no config. So the repo now carries the same typeface family twice, ~275 KB total, one copy dead.

This matters under two of the project's own rules: CLAUDE.md's heavy-files policy ('No images, videos, or office binaries in git', with the repo going public for CI and clones expected to stay lean), and R15 'Dead weight is not ported'. Separately, `spec.md:45`'s residual row says the CLAUDE.md amendment should name `public/brand` + `public/marketing` as required build assets — it does not name `apps/web/fonts/`, which is equally a new tracked binary directory and will trip the same policy on the next audit.

Note: the dead `app/fonts/*.woff` pair predates this change; the defect this change contributes is the duplicate plus the incomplete residual.
findings.fixHint: Delete the unreferenced apps/web/app/fonts/GeistVF.woff and GeistMonoVF.woff, and add apps/web/fonts/ to the spec's CLAUDE.md heavy-files residual alongside public/brand and public/marketing.
findings.decision: The port adds 141 KB of Geist woff2 while a 134 KB tracked woff copy of the same family sits unreferenced under app/fonts/, so the repo carries the family twice against R15's dead-weight rule and the heavy-files policy, and the spec's residual row does not name the new directory. The stale copy predates the port, but the port was the moment to replace rather than duplicate it.

confirmedFindings.summary: Adding `/` to the mobile-proxy skip list makes the signed-in landing redirect fire on phones for the first time, sending them to `/dashboard` or `/buyer/portal` — paths the mobile-web build has no route for.
confirmedFindings.detail: Before the change, a phone request for `/` returned at line 83 (`NextResponse.rewrite(proxyTarget)`) and the mobile-web build did its own role routing; the landing-redirect block at line 99 was unreachable on mobile (the comment at line 94 still says exactly that: "Runs AFTER the mobile-UA proxy so phones land in the mobile-web build"). Now `isMarketingPath('/')` is true, so `skipMobileRedirect` is true, the rewrite is skipped, and execution reaches line 99. Concrete failure: an operator on an iPhone with `rf-op-auth=1` opens https://www.routeflow.info/ → 307 to `/dashboard` → the browser re-requests `/dashboard`, which is NOT in MARKETING_PATHS, so the middleware rewrites it to `${MOBILE_WEB_URL}/dashboard`. `apps/mobile/app/` contains only `(auth)`, `(customer)`, `(driver)`, `(operator)`, `(tenant)` and `index.tsx` — there is no `dashboard` or `buyer/portal` route and no `+not-found.tsx`; apps/mobile/Dockerfile's nginx does `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html`, so the SPA loads and expo-router lands on its Unmatched Route screen instead of the role-routed app. Same for a buyer (`rf-buyer-auth=1`) → `/buyer/portal`. Nothing pins this: the new middleware.marketing.test.ts sends no presence cookies, and CC-11…CC-15 in e2e/05-cross-cutting.spec.ts run under a desktop project.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either keep proxying `/` to the mobile-web build when a presence cookie is set (evaluate `resolveLandingTarget` before the marketing skip, and only skip the proxy when it returns null), or exclude `/` from MARKETING_PATHS and handle signed-out mobile `/` explicitly. Also fix the now-false comment at line 94.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` metadata routes are absent from MARKETING_PATHS, so any mobile user agent gets the mobile-web SPA's HTML instead of the robots/sitemap body.
confirmedFindings.detail: `app/robots.ts` and `app/sitemap.ts` are new in this change (untracked in `git status`) and serve `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml`. The middleware matcher `/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)` covers both paths, neither is in MARKETING_PATHS, so `skipMobileRedirect` is false and `isMobileUserAgent` — `/Mobi|Android|iPhone|iPod|BlackBerry|IEMobile|Opera Mini/i` — matches. Concrete failure: a request for https://www.routeflow.info/robots.txt with the Googlebot-Smartphone UA (which contains both "Android" and "Mobile") is rewritten to `${MOBILE_WEB_URL}/robots.txt`; apps/mobile/Dockerfile's nginx `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html` returns the Expo SPA index.html as text/html. The same happens for `/sitemap.xml` and for any phone user opening those URLs. R10's "SEO stance is production" therefore does not hold for the mobile-first crawler that the rest of R11 was written to accommodate.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add "/robots.txt" and "/sitemap.xml" to MARKETING_PATHS (and extend the T11 unit table with them so the pin exists).

confirmedFindings.summary: Adding `/` to MARKETING_PATHS makes the signed-in landing redirect fire for phones for the first time, sending them to `/dashboard` or `/buyer/portal`, which are then proxied to mobile-web paths that do not exist in the Expo app.

confirmedFindings.summary: The brand mark PNGs have no alpha channel and the `mix-blend-mode: multiply` that hides the white ground is scoped to `.rf-marketing` only, so the mark renders as an opaque white square on every dark non-marketing surface.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified with sharp: public/brand/routeflow-mark-{64,180,192,512}.png are PNG colour type 2 (RGB), `hasAlpha: false`, no tRNS chunk; sampled pixels at (0,0), (191,0), (0,191) are [255,255,255]. The only compensating rule is `.rf-marketing .brand-mark { mix-blend-mode: multiply }` at marketing.css:9707, which cannot apply outside the marketing wrapper. Failure scenario: a platform admin opens /admin — the sidebar is `bg-slate-900` and BrandMark (line 89) paints a 32×32 opaque white tile where an indigo rounded Shield box used to be. Same on app/buyer/portal/layout.tsx:254 (sidebar `bg-gradient-to-b from-buyer-900 to-buyer-800`), app/buyer/login/page.tsx:105 (emerald gradient panel) and app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:231 (BrandSignature 48 px on the dark teal/navy gradient). ux-spec §2 assumed "On dark backgrounds … the PNG is used as-is", which only works where the multiply blend is applied. P2 flagged this risk; it was not addressed and is not covered by any test (T4 only checks src/alt/aria-hidden).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either regenerate the four PNGs with a real alpha channel (transparent ground) or add a global `.brand-mark { mix-blend-mode: multiply }` — note multiply on a dark ground darkens the mark to invisibility, so alpha is the safer fix; then re-check the four dark surfaces.

confirmedFindings.summary: The only desktop-UA pin uses /pricing, which the change now exempts unconditionally, so it passes regardless of the UA check — nothing in the suite guards mobile-UA detection returning true for desktop.

The pin `does not rewrite /pricing for a desktop UA (MKT-PIN T11)` therefore asserts a value produced before `isMobileUserAgent(ua)` is ever consulted. The desktop branch of a HIGH-risk auth/routing file has zero executed coverage. Related uncovered branches in the same file: the `?desktop=1` / `prefer-desktop` cookie opt-out the plan lists as an input, and the documented "exact-path match only, so a marketing-looking sub-route stays subject to the proxy" claim (e.g. /product/anything) — neither has a test.

confirmedFindings.summary: Exempting "/" from the mobile-UA proxy re-enables the signed-in landing redirect for phones, sending them to /dashboard or /buyer/portal — paths the mobile-web build has no route for.
confirmedFindings.detail: Before this change `isMarketingPath` did not exist, so a mobile UA hitting "/" was rewritten to MOBILE_WEB_URL and `middleware` returned at line 83 — the landing block at lines 97-121 was unreachable on phones. Now "/" is in MARKETING_PATHS, so a phone that carries `rf-op-auth` or `rf-buyer-auth` falls through to `resolveLandingTarget`, which returns "/dashboard" or "/buyer/portal" (apps/web/lib/portal-routing.ts:67-76), and the browser's follow-up request for that path IS proxied to the mobile build. `find apps/mobile/app` shows no `dashboard` and no `portal` route — the Expo routes are (auth)/(customer)/(driver)/(operator)/(tenant), whose groups are URL-transparent. Failure scenario: a phone browser whose 30-day `prefer-desktop` cookie has lapsed while `rf-op-auth` kept sliding on token refresh opens www.routeflow.info/ and gets 307 -> /dashboard -> proxied to <mobile>/dashboard, which the mobile build cannot route; previously that same request served the mobile landing screen.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the intended phone behaviour for a signed-in visitor on "/": either keep the landing redirect skipped for mobile UAs, or point it at a path the mobile-web build actually serves.

confirmedFindings.summary: Adding "/" to MARKETING_PATHS lets signed-in phone users fall through to the landing 307, which sends them to /dashboard or /buyer/portal — paths the mobile-web build has no route for.
confirmedFindings.detail: Before this change, `skipMobileRedirect` was false for "/", so a mobile UA hit the rewrite at middleware.ts:74-85 and was proxied to the mobile-web build's "/", which does its own role-based routing (`git show HEAD:apps/web/middleware.ts` confirms the same block order — only the skip condition changed). The in-file comment at middleware.ts:94-95 ("Runs AFTER the mobile-UA proxy so phones land in the mobile-web build, which does its own role-based routing") is now false and was not updated. confirmedFindings.summary: T5's BANNED_DEPENDENCIES demands apps/web drop `recharts` and `react-day-picker`, but both are live production dependencies imported by 10 dashboard/buyer-portal files — the final gate is red today and satisfying the assertion would break the build.

confirmedFindings.detail: `od -c` on lines 34 and 85 of the spec shows byte 0x27 (`Let's talk about...`, `Let's get you back on track.`). `od -c` on apps/web/app/(marketing)/contact/page.tsx:46 and apps/web/app/not-found.tsx:19 shows \342\200\231 (U+2019 ’). Playwright's toHaveText normalises whitespace only — it does not fold quote characters. Failure scenario: T1 for /contact and the "bogus marketing path 404s" test both fail on `Expected: "Let's..." Received: "Let’s..."` against a correctly-ported page.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Use the typographic ’ in both expected strings (lines 34 and 85) to match the rendered copy.

confirmedFindings.summary:
T12 asserts the raw /pricing HTML body contains the joined h1 string, but the served markup splits it across a
and an .

your working day.`. That substring is never present. Failure scenario: T12 — the only test proving the mobile-UA carve-out (R11) actually serves marketing rather than the mobile build — fails on a correctly-working deploy, so the middleware change's post-deploy proof is unusable.

confirmedFindings.summary: T2 clicks the desktop "Sign in" dropdown at the iPhone 13 viewport, where marketing.css hides `.nav-login` entirely.
confirmedFindings.detail: The describe block does `test.use({ ...iPhone13 })`; `devices["iPhone 13"].viewport` is {width:390,height:664} (read from @playwright/test in this session). Enumerating every `.nav-login` rule in apps/web/app/(marketing)/marketing.css in file order gives: line 724 `@media (max-width:800px) { display:none }`, line 2644 `@media (max-width:900px) { display:block }`, line 3105 `@media (max-width:480px) { display:none }`. All three match at 390 px and all have identical specificity, so the last one wins: the Sign in trigger is `display:none`. Failure scenario: `page.getByRole("button", { name: /sign in/i }).click()` matches no element in the accessibility tree (display:none is excluded) and the test times out, even though the mobile sheet — which the previous test already covers — carries both sign-in links by design.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the intended behaviour: either run this assertion at a desktop/tablet viewport (the dropdown is deliberately hidden below 480 px, with the sheet carrying both links), or change the CSS so `.nav-login` stays visible at phone widths.

confirmedFindings.summary: T2 targets a WorkflowTour tab named "Routes" that does not exist — the ported tab labels are "Take the order" / "Plan the route" / "Confirm delivery" / "Follow the account".

Grepping apps/web/app/(marketing)/wholesalers/page.tsx confirms WorkflowTour is the only tablist on that page. The test-plan row ("click the 'Routes' tab ... tab panel 'routes' visible") was written against the step ids, not the rendered labels.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Target the real label, e.g. `getByRole("tab", { name: /plan the route/i })`, and assert the panel that opens.

confirmedFindings.summary: The shared brand mark PNG is opaque white with no alpha, and the `mix-blend-mode: multiply` that hides that is scoped to `.rf-marketing`, so every dark non-marketing surface now shows a solid white square.
confirmedFindings.detail: Decoded apps/web/public/brand/routeflow-mark-64.png in this session: PNG colorType 2 (truecolor, no alpha); all four corners and the centre read [255,255,255]. All four sizes are colorType 2. The compensating rule is `.rf-marketing .brand-mark { mix-blend-mode: multiply }` at apps/web/app/(marketing)/marketing.css:9705-9708 — there is no `.brand-mark` rule anywhere outside `.rf-marketing` (grep over app/globals.css and packages/ui returns nothing). Failure scenario: on the four dark surfaces this change points at BRAND_MARK_SRC the mark paints as an opaque white box — the login page's #0E1F36 gradient panel (app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:231, which replaced a hand-tuned cream-on-dark SVG whose deleted comment explicitly said the light-bg asset 'would render with poor contrast against this panel'), the platform-admin `bg-slate-900` sidebar (app/(platform-admin)/layout.tsx:89), the buyer portal `bg-gradient-to-b from-buyer-900` sidebar (app/buyer/portal/layout.tsx:254), and the operator `bg-navy` sidebar for any tenant with no custom logoUrl (app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:1309 via TenantLogo's new fallback). Both PWA manifests also declare `purpose: "any maskable"` on this opaque icon. Note `mix-blend-mode: multiply` cannot be the fix outside marketing: on a dark ground it drives the whole mark toward the background colour.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Re-export the mark with a real alpha channel (or ship a dark-surface variant) before pointing dark shells at it; the P2 engineer flagged the missing alpha explicitly and it was left unaddressed.

confirmedFindings.summary: The R-MKT gate demands `recharts` and `react-day-picker` be removed from apps/web/package.json, but both are live dependencies of the operator dashboard, platform-admin and buyer portal — the gate cannot be made green without breaking the app.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified by running `cd apps/web && npx jest --silent`: `Test Suites: 1 failed, 37 passed, 38 total / Tests: 2 failed, 259 passed` — the ONLY two failures in the whole workspace are `apps/web/package.json has no recharts dependency (R-MKT T5)` and `...no react-day-picker dependency (R-MKT T5)`. Both packages are imported by shipped, non-marketing source: `recharts` at (dashboard)/analytics/page.tsx:13, (dashboard)/compliance/[categoryId]/page.tsx:15, (dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx:59, (dashboard)/finance/reports/page.tsx:46, (dashboard)/products/[id]/DemandCard.tsx:4, (dashboard)/products/[id]/page.tsx:30, (platform-admin)/admin/dashboard/page.tsx:22, buyer/portal/[seller]/finances/page.tsx:15, components/ReportChart.tsx:18; `react-day-picker` at components/DateRangePicker.tsx:5-6 (including `import "react-day-picker/style.css"`). Failure scenario: to satisfy the gate an engineer deletes the two deps from apps/web/package.json — the next `npm ci` + `next build` then fails to resolve 10 modules and every chart in the analytics/compliance/finance/product/platform-admin/buyer-finances pages plus every date-range picker dies. Leave the deps in and the build-plan's own `final` gate (`cd apps/web && npx jest --silent`) stays red, so the change cannot land as specified. Spec R15's intent was 'do not PORT the redesign's dependencies', which the test over-generalised into 'apps/web must not have them at all'. No work package in build-plan.md owns apps/web/package.json, which is why every implementation engineer reported this row as out-of-scope rather than fixing it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Scope the assertion to what R15 actually means (e.g. no NEW import of recharts/react-day-picker under app/(marketing)/**, or drop the two rows from BANNED_DEPENDENCIES and keep only the PINNED_ABSENT_DEPENDENCIES list). Do NOT delete the dependencies from apps/web/package.json.

confirmedFindings.summary: The one shared brand mark is an opaque white-background PNG with no alpha channel, and the `mix-blend-mode: multiply` that hides that background is scoped to `.rf-marketing` only — so it renders as a solid white square on all four dark app surfaces.
confirmedFindings.detail: I decoded the PNGs: all four `apps/web/public/brand/routeflow-mark-{64,180,192,512}.png` have IHDR colorType=2 (truecolor, NO alpha channel), and the decoded corner pixels of the 64px file are 255,255,255 — a solid white background. The only rule that neutralises that is `.rf-marketing .brand-mark { object-fit: contain; mix-blend-mode: multiply; ... }` at app/(marketing)/marketing.css:9705-9709; `grep 'brand-mark' apps/web/app/globals.css` returns nothing, so outside the `.rf-marketing` wrapper the raw white raster is what paints. Concrete dark-surface consumers: (platform-admin)/layout.tsx:89 `<BrandMark size={32}>` inside `<aside className="...bg-slate-900...">`; buyer/portal/layout.tsx:254 `<BrandMark size={32}>` inside `bg-gradient-to-b from-buyer-900 to-buyer-800`; (dashboard)/layout.tsx:1309 and :1358 `<TenantLogo className="h-8 w-8">` inside `bg-navy`, whose fallback is now BRAND_MARK_SRC (components/TenantLogo.tsx:35) for every tenant with no uploaded `branding.logoUrl`; (auth)/login/page.tsx:231 `<BrandSignature size={48}>` on the dark teal/navy panel; buyer/login/page.tsx:105 inside a `bg-white/10` tile. Failure scenario: on deploy day every operator without a tenant logo, every buyer portal user, every platform admin, and everyone on the two login screens sees a 32-48 px solid white box where the logo used to be. The diff's own removed code documents the hazard — the deleted login SVG carried the comment "The shared /logo.svg asset is the light-bg version ... which would render with poor contrast against this panel's #0E1F36 gradient" — and the P2 engineer flagged the missing dark treatment explicitly. build-plan.md's owner-verification line ("confirm the mark reads well on the dashboard's dark sidebar and the login panel") anticipated it, but nothing in the code addresses it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either ship the mark with a real alpha channel (transparent background) so it composites on any surface, or add an unscoped `.brand-mark { mix-blend-mode: multiply }`-equivalent dark treatment / light chip behind the mark on the four dark surfaces. Confirm the intended accent colour for `.brand-period` outside `.rf-marketing` at the same time (BrandMark.tsx:44 hardcodes #10264d, overridden ad hoc to #7DDCD8 on login only).

confirmedFindings.summary: Production /privacy and /terms ship <title>, description and OG copy that call the live site a "design preview", even though the page bodies were correctly de-previewed.
confirmedFindings.detail: site.ts:68-69 and :74-75 carry `title: "Privacy information for this preview"` / `description: "Important information about the RouteFlow website design preview."` and `title: "Terms information for this preview"` / `description: "Preview status and legal review requirements for the RouteFlow redesign."`. app/(marketing)/privacy/page.tsx:14-24 and terms/page.tsx feed those straight into `metadata.title`, `metadata.description` AND `metadata.openGraph.{title,description}`. Failure scenario: a visitor clicks Privacy in the footer of the live site and the browser tab reads "Privacy information for this preview · RouteFlow"; pasting the /privacy or /terms link into Slack/WhatsApp/iMessage unfurls with "Important information about the RouteFlow website design preview." — `robots: { index: false }` blocks search indexing but does not suppress OG unfurls. The rest of the port removed this framing deliberately: spec R2 lists "Website design preview · Review status" as a preview-only line to drop, R9 supplies the interim body copy (which both pages use correctly), and e2e/36-marketing-site.spec.ts's header states "R9 deliberately supersedes M1 §2g's preview-banner placeholder text" — the two metadata rows were simply missed, and site.ts:7's comment records the omission as intentional.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Replace the two preview-worded titles/descriptions in site.ts:66-77 with production copy matching the R9 bodies (e.g. "Privacy information" / "Our privacy policy is being finalised — contact hello@routeflow.info."), and update site.ts:5-8's comment.

confirmedFindings.summary: R15/T5's "apps/web/package.json has no recharts / react-day-picker dependency" is unsatisfiable and no work package owns apps/web/package.json, so the red gate can never go green.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified by running the gate: `cd apps/web && npx jest --runInBand -t "R-MKT"` ends `Tests: 2 failed, 196 skipped, 63 passed` and the full `npx jest --silent` ends `Tests: 2 failed, 259 passed` — both failures are exactly these two rows (BANNED_DEPENDENCIES at marketing-port.static.test.ts:147). No package in build-plan.md P1–P6 lists apps/web/package.json, which is why both P2 and P4 reported it as unclaimed scope. Worse, the requirement is wrong on the merits: `recharts` is imported by live dashboard code (apps/web/components/ReportChart.tsx, app/(dashboard)/analytics/page.tsx, finance/reports/page.tsx, customers/[id]/page.tsx, products/[id]/page.tsx + DemandCard.tsx, compliance/[categoryId]/page.tsx, (platform-admin)/admin/dashboard/page.tsx, buyer/portal/[seller]/finances/page.tsx) and `react-day-picker` by apps/web/components/DateRangePicker.tsx (grep run this session). Anyone who "fixes" the red row by deleting the deps breaks `next build` for the whole dashboard. Either the requirement/test rows are retired (they belong to the redesign's dependency set, not this app's) or a package must own package.json — right now neither is true.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Drop the two rows from BANNED_DEPENDENCIES (move them to a comment explaining both deps are load-bearing dashboard deps), or amend R15 in spec.md; do NOT remove the dependencies.

confirmedFindings.summary: The brand mark PNG has no alpha channel and its mix-blend-mode fix exists only under .rf-marketing, so the mark renders as an opaque white square on the dark platform-admin sidebar and login panel.
confirmedFindings.detail: All four files under apps/web/public/brand/ are PNG colorType 2 (truecolor, no alpha) — verified this session by reading the IHDR bytes of routeflow-mark-{64,180,192,512}.png. The only compensating rule is `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on `.rf-marketing .brand-mark` (apps/web/app/(marketing)/marketing.css:9705-9707 and the other .rf-marketing-scoped copies); `grep brand-mark apps/web/app/globals.css` returns nothing, and globals.css is byte-pinned by MKT-PIN T7 so no package can add a global rule. BrandMark is now rendered on non-marketing dark surfaces: app/(platform-admin)/layout.tsx:89 places `<BrandMark size={32}>` inside an `aside` with `bg-slate-900`, and app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:231 places `<BrandSignature size={48}>` on the dark #0E1F36 gradient panel (replacing an inline SVG that existed precisely because "the shared /logo.svg asset … would render with poor contrast against this panel"). Result: a white/light square behind the mark on both surfaces. No work package owns styling for `.brand-mark` outside `.rf-marketing`; the P2 engineer flagged this and it remained unassigned. The same gap leaves `.brand-signature`/`.brand-wordmark` completely unstyled on app/not-found.tsx's siblings and any non-marketing use.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Ship the mark with transparency (re-export as RGBA PNG or SVG), or add a non-marketing `.brand-mark` rule in a scoped stylesheet the brand component imports — globals.css is pinned, so it cannot go there.

confirmedFindings.summary: /privacy and /terms ship preview-era <title> and description to production, contradicting R2's drop-preview-copy rule and R9's production legal shells.
confirmedFindings.detail: site.ts:66-76 sets privacy `title: "Privacy information for this preview"` / `description: "Important information about the RouteFlow website design preview."` and terms `title: "Terms information for this preview"` / `description: "Preview status and legal review requirements for the RouteFlow redesign."`. Those strings drive each route's `metadata` (and therefore the browser tab, share cards, and any crawler that follows the footer link — R9 sets `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`, not noindex-for-humans). Spec R2 explicitly requires the preview-only lines to be dropped and R9 requires production legal shells; the file's own comment acknowledges it kept "preview-authored copy". apps/web/app/(marketing)/seo.test.ts:49-53 asserts these exact strings, so the test locks the defect in rather than catching it. Failure scenario: a real prospect opens the footer's Privacy link and the tab reads "Privacy information for this preview · RouteFlow" on the live www.routeflow.info site.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Replace both titles/descriptions with production copy matching the R9 body (e.g. "Privacy information" / "How RouteFlow handles your data") and update the two pinned strings in seo.test.ts.

confirmedFindings.summary: The shared brand mark PNG is opaque RGB with a solid white background, so every dark surface outside `.rf-marketing` now renders a white square behind the mark.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified with sharp/PNG header parsing in this session: `apps/web/public/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png` is colorType 2 (truecolor, no alpha channel), carries no `tRNS` chunk, and its corner pixels are (255,255,255) — fully opaque white. The 64/180/512 derivatives are colorType 2 as well. The only compensating rule in the diff is `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, and it is scoped `.rf-marketing .brand-mark` (apps/web/app/(marketing)/marketing.css:9705), so it never applies outside the marketing route group. Concrete failures: (1) `app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:231` renders `<BrandSignature size={48}>` inside the left panel's dark `#0E1F36` teal/navy gradient — the diff deleted a transparent inline SVG that had been authored specifically for that panel, so a 48px solid white square now sits where the arc mark was; (2) `app/(platform-admin)/layout.tsx:89` renders `<BrandMark size={32} className="rounded-lg">` inside an `aside className="…bg-slate-900…"`; (3) `app/buyer/portal/layout.tsx:254` renders it inside `aside className="…bg-gradient-to-b from-buyer-900 to-buyer-800…"`; (4) `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:1309` and `:1358` render `TenantLogo` (fallback now `BRAND_MARK_SRC`, components/TenantLogo.tsx:35) inside the `bg-navy` sidebar and mobile drawer, so any tenant with no `branding.logoUrl` gets a white 32px box on navy. `sharp` IS present in node_modules (verified), so an alpha-channel variant is derivable.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Emit an alpha-channel (colorType 6) variant of the mark — either by keying out the white background with sharp, or by shipping a second cream/white-on-dark asset — and use it (or apply the same blend treatment) at the four dark sites above.

confirmedFindings.summary: The native `<details>/<summary>` FAQ has no matching layout CSS: the browser disclosure triangle is left visible, the chevron is not right-aligned or rotated, there are no item dividers, and the open/close animation is absent.
confirmedFindings.detail: The port swapped shadcn's Accordion (which carried its layout in Tailwind utility classes on the component) for native `<details>/<summary>` but only the `data-slot` colour/spacing rules were carried into marketing.css. Verified by grepping every `.faq-list` rule in apps/web/app/(marketing)/marketing.css (lines 1525, 1534, 1539, 2876, 2880, 4998, 5001, 5005, 5511, 6208): (a) `.faq-list [data-slot="accordion-trigger"]` (1525) sets `align-items:center` but never `display:flex`/`justify-content:space-between`, so on a block-level `<summary>` `align-items` is inert and the `<ChevronDown>` at faq.tsx:87 sits inline immediately after the question text instead of at the right edge; (b) there is no `list-style:none` or `::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}` for `summary` anywhere in the file (the three `list-style:none` occurrences are `.check-list`, `.getting-started ol/.retailer-start ol`, `.ai-review-steps`), so the browser's default disclosure triangle renders alongside the chevron; (c) `.faq-list [data-slot="accordion-item"]` (4998) sets `border-color` but no element in faq.tsx carries that attribute — the selector matches nothing, and `.faq-list` itself has no rule, so there are no dividers or gaps between the five items; (d) nothing keys off the open state (grep for `data-state` returns only `.tour-tabs` rules), so the chevron never rotates and the grid-rows panel animation ux-spec §4 requires is absent — `[data-slot="accordion-content"] > div { height: auto !important }` (1539) is the leftover of the animation that was dropped. This FAQ ships on `/`, `/product` and `/retailers`.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add the missing summary rules under `.rf-marketing .faq-list`: `summary{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;list-style:none}` + `summary::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}`, a `details` border/divider, `details[open] summary svg{transform:rotate(180deg)}`, and either the grid-rows transition or an explicit decision to ship without it.

confirmedFindings.summary: The privacy and terms routes ship preview-era titles and descriptions to production, describing the live site as a design preview.
confirmedFindings.detail: routes[] carries `title: "Privacy information for this preview"` / `description: "Important information about the RouteFlow website design preview."` (lines 68-69) and `title: "Terms information for this preview"` / `description: "Preview status and legal review requirements for the RouteFlow redesign."` (lines 74-75). Those strings are consumed by app/(marketing)/privacy/page.tsx:14 and terms/page.tsx:14 for `<title>`, `description` and the OpenGraph card, so a visitor on the production site sees the browser tab read "Privacy information for this preview · RouteFlow", and any link preview repeats "RouteFlow website design preview". Spec R2 explicitly drops preview-only lines and R9 rewrote the page bodies to interim production copy; the metadata was left behind. seo.test.ts:48-55 pins the same strings, so the fix has to update both files together.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Rewrite the two rows to production copy (e.g. "Privacy information" / "Terms information" with a neutral description) and update the matching EXPECTED_ROUTE_METADATA entries in app/(marketing)/seo.test.ts.

confirmedFindings.summary: `restart()` does not reset the two fields the user actually edited — quantity and route — although the spec's reverse-action sweep says Restart resets quantity/route/delivered/paid.
confirmedFindings.detail: The forward path writes five pieces of state: `chapter`, `quantity` (adjust, line 221), `route` (assign, line 227), `delivered` and `paid` (confirm / Record sample payment). `restart()` at lines 239-244 sets only `chapter`, `delivered`, `paid` and `playing`. spec.md's "Reverse of every action" line states "the story's Restart resets quantity/route/delivered/paid". Concrete failure: a visitor sets 12 cases, assigns the East run, confirms delivery, records payment, then presses the Restart control (site-header of the story, line 594, aria-label "Restart the sample order story"); chapter 1 reopens still showing 12 cases and, at chapter 3, still assigned to the East run, so the replay is not the clean sample story the copy promises.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `setQuantity(4); setRoute(0);` to restart() (4 and 0 are the initial values at lines 162-163) — or, if the redesign deliberately preserved them, correct the spec sentence instead.

confirmedFindings.summary: BrandMark imports `cn` from the root `@routeflow/ui` barrel instead of `@routeflow/ui/web`, pulling the whole web component set into every marketing page's module graph.
confirmedFindings.detail: `import { cn } from "@routeflow/ui"` resolves to packages/ui/index.tsx, which does `export * from "./src/web/index"` — a barrel re-exporting Modal, Toast, Table, Select, Tabs and friends, all of them `"use client"` Radix components. packages/ui/package.json declares no `sideEffects` field, so webpack cannot safely drop those modules from the graph. BrandMark is the only file under apps/web that imports the root barrel (`grep -rln 'from "@routeflow/ui"' apps/web` returns it alone); every other consumer imports `@routeflow/ui/web`, and `cn` is exported from that subpath too (packages/ui/src/web/index.ts). Since BrandMark is rendered by the marketing layout's header/footer and by app/not-found.tsx, the cost lands on the public pages the port exists to make fast. I could not measure the resulting bundle: `npx next build` aborts in this worktree with a pre-existing `ReactCurrentDispatcher` error from the react@18/19 nesting documented in apps/web/jest.config.js, which is unrelated to this change.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Change the import to `from "@routeflow/ui/web"`, matching every other apps/web consumer.

confirmedFindings.summary: The mobile sheet omits the "Book a demo" CTA that ux-spec §3 requires, and the header button is CSS-hidden below 480 px, leaving phones with no primary CTA in the chrome.
confirmedFindings.detail: ux-spec.md §3 specifies the ≤960 px sheet "listing the five items + Contact + both sign-ins + Book a demo". The `.mobile-access` block (lines 118-125) contains only the two sign-in links; the nav above adds the five routes plus Contact, for 8 links. Meanwhile marketing.css line 3102-3104 sets `.rf-marketing .header-actions > .button { display: none }` under `@media (max-width: 480px)`, which is the "Book a demo" Link at site-header.tsx:82. Failure scenario: a visitor on a 390 px phone sees no "Book a demo" button in the header and none in the opened sheet; the only route to /contact is the plain "Contact" nav link. e2e/36-marketing-site.spec.ts:145 asserts `toHaveCount(8)` on the sheet's links, encoding the omission so it can never be caught.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add a "Book a demo" link (href="/contact") to the `.mobile-access` block in site-header.tsx and bump the expected sheet link count in e2e/36-marketing-site.spec.ts:129-145 from 8 to 9.

confirmedFindings.summary: The story's Restart does not reset quantity or route, contrary to spec.md's completeness sweep.
confirmedFindings.detail: spec.md "Reverse of every action" states "the story's Restart resets quantity/route/delivered/paid". `restart` (lines 239-244) sets only `setChapter(0)`, `setDelivered(false)`, `setPaid(false)`, `setPlaying(true)`. Failure scenario: a visitor raises the quantity to 12 cases and assigns the "East run", presses Restart, and chapter 1 re-opens still showing 12 cases and the East run instead of the documented reset state (4 cases, North run). No test covers Restart — T8a only exercises the pure model's `exampleOrder`/`nextChapter`.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `setQuantity(4); setRoute(0);` to `restart` (or amend the spec line if the redesign's behaviour is intentionally partial and record it as a deviation).

confirmedFindings.summary: marketing.css is 9,776 lines against ux-spec §1's "Target ≤ 3,500 lines" and its instruction to drop duplicated declarations; the unconsolidated duplicates produce contradictory breakpoint behaviour and the overrun was not reported as a deviation.
confirmedFindings.detail: `wc -l` gives 9,776 (2.8× the stated ceiling). ux-spec §1 asked to "port the rules that actually paint, drop dead/duplicated declarations"; instead the ten source stylesheets were concatenated in source order (file header lines 3-8 says so). Concrete consequence: `.rf-marketing .nav-login` gets three conflicting `display` values across overlapping breakpoints (marketing.css:725 none @≤800, :2645 block @≤900, :3106 none @≤480) and `.rf-marketing .site-footer` gets three different backgrounds (:1598 #f6f8fb, :5454 #f3f6fbd9, :8745 #f5f5f7). The 800/900 pair is self-cancelling dead weight, and the ≤480 rule is what silently breaks the T2 sign-in test. P2's deviation note did not mention the line-count overrun.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: De-duplicate the concatenated blocks (at minimum collapse the contradictory .nav-login / .desktop-nav / .site-footer duplicates into one breakpoint ladder) or record the overrun as an accepted deviation with the owner.

confirmedFindings.summary: BrandSignature paints the period with an inline style, which outranks every ported `.brand-period` rule and makes the footer's own period colour dead.
confirmedFindings.detail: Line 58 renders `<span className="brand-period" style={{ color: periodColor }}>` with `periodColor` defaulting to the literal `#10264d`. An inline style beats any class rule, so both `.rf-marketing .brand-period { color: var(--primary) }` (marketing.css:964) and `.rf-marketing .site-footer .brand-period { color: #8a8496 }` (marketing.css:8382) never take effect. Failure scenario: the footer's brand signature renders its period in navy #10264d instead of the ported #8a8496, and a future change to the marketing `--primary` token would silently not reach the wordmark period. ux-spec §2 states the period should be `var(--primary)` inside `.rf-marketing`.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Only emit the inline style when a `periodColor` prop is explicitly passed (drop DEFAULT_PERIOD_COLOR and let the CSS rules win inside .rf-marketing), keeping the login page's explicit #7DDCD8 override.

confirmedFindings.summary: T8a exercises only the happy path of exampleOrder — the cases clamp and the `paid && delivered` coupling are unasserted.
confirmedFindings.detail: operation-model.ts:53-71 clamps `cases` to [1,12] with a non-finite fallback of 4, and computes `isPaid = Boolean(paid && isDelivered)` so a paid-but-undelivered order still carries the full balance. The test only calls `exampleOrder(4, {delivered:false,paid:false})` and `exampleOrder(4, {delivered:true,paid:true})`. Failure scenario: delete `&& isDelivered` (or the Math.max/Math.min clamp, so `exampleOrder(0)` yields total 42 and `available: 148`) and every T8a row still passes — the demo would show a zero balance for an order that was paid but never delivered, and the suite would not notice.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add rows for `exampleOrder(4,{delivered:false,paid:true}).balance === 114` and for the clamp (`exampleOrder(0).cases === 1`, `exampleOrder(99).cases === 12`).

GENERAL : RETAILER`) and the retailers page ships the wrong four/five questions with a fully green suite; the unit assertion `toHaveLength(5)` would still pass on the general set.

confirmedFindings.summary: DemoForm's tests cover only the success path — R8's "never submits or stores anything" and the required-field/empty-input path are unasserted.
confirmedFindings.detail: demo-form.tsx renders the disclosure "It does not submit or store your request" and relies on `event.preventDefault()` plus required inputs; no test asserts that no network call is made, and no test submits with empty fields. Failure scenario: someone adds a `fetch("/api/leads", …)` to the submit handler (or drops `event.preventDefault()`, causing a real form navigation) and all five R-MKT T8c rows still pass, silently turning a mailto-only marketing form into a lead-capture endpoint — the explicit non-goal in spec.md.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Assert `global.fetch` (spied) was not called after submit, and add a case that submitting the empty form does not reach the draft-ready heading.

confirmedFindings.summary: OperationStory's Restart does not reset `quantity` or `route`, contradicting the spec's stated reverse-of-action.
confirmedFindings.detail: spec.md's completeness sweep (line 36) states "the story's Restart resets quantity/route/delivered/paid". `restart()` sets chapter 0, delivered false, paid false and playing true, but leaves `quantity` and `route` at whatever the visitor last chose. Failure scenario: a visitor raises the case count to 12 and assigns the East run, then presses the Restart control (aria-label "Restart the sample order story"); the story returns to chapter 1 still showing 12 cases and the East run, so the "restart" does not restore the initial illustrative state the copy and spec describe.
