confirmedFindings.summary: `BrandMark`'s `size` prop is overridden by marketing.css on every `.rf-marketing` surface, so the 404 mark renders at 30 px instead of the planned 40 px, and its `not-found-brand` class has no CSS rule at all.
confirmedFindings.detail: marketing.css declares `.rf-marketing .brand-mark { width: 34px; height: 34px; ... }` at line 163 and then re-declares `.rf-marketing .brand-mark { width: 30px; height: 30px; }` at line 4401 (the redesign's stylesheets were concatenated without dedup); equal specificity means the later 30 px wins for every plain `.brand-mark` at desktop width. `BrandMark` (components/brand/BrandMark.tsx:18-28) applies `size` only as next/image's width/height attributes plus the `brand-mark` class, so the CSS wins in the browser. not-found.tsx:13 passes `size={40}`, which build-plan.md P1 specifies ("404: `BrandMark` 40 px + wordmark") — it will paint at 30 px. The `className="not-found-brand"` passed alongside lands on the wrapping `<Link>` and matches nothing: `grep -n "not-found-brand" app/(marketing)/marketing.css` exits 1 with no match. The same silent override applies to `<BrandMark />` in conversion-sections.tsx:122 and `<BrandSignature />` in operation-story.tsx:274 / product/page.tsx:98. Note this makes components/brand/BrandMark.test.tsx's size assertions non-predictive: they pass in jsdom (no stylesheet) while the browser renders a different size.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either drop the duplicate `.rf-marketing .brand-mark` width block (marketing.css:163 or :4401) and let the component's size attributes drive, or have BrandMark emit an inline width/height style so `size` beats the class rule. Remove or implement the dead `not-found-brand` class.

confirmedFindings.summary: The T8b single-open assertion is racy against the async <details> toggle event and failed once in the red gate this session.
confirmedFindings.detail: Observed directly: the first `cd apps/web && npx jest --runInBand -t "R-MKT"` run of this session failed with `expect(openItems).toHaveLength(1) … Received length: 2` (both the second and third <details> carried `open`); four subsequent runs (`-t "R-MKT T8b"` x3 and `-t "R-MKT"` x2, plus the full `npx jest --silent`) passed. Cause: faq.tsx:80 drives `open={openIndex === i}` from an `onToggle` handler, and the DOM `toggle` event on <details> is dispatched asynchronously, so the second `await user.click(...)` can land before React has re-rendered the first item closed. The test has no waitFor/findBy around the post-click read, so the red gate is intermittently red for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Wrap the open-count read in `await waitFor(...)` (or assert via findByRole on the expanded panel) so the assertion retries past the queued toggle event.

confirmedFindings.summary: Two competing global focus-ring rules ship different colours, and neither uses the `--ring` token the token table declares.
confirmedFindings.detail: marketing.css:87-92 sets `.rf-marketing a|button|input|textarea|summary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #245be8; outline-offset: 5px }`, while marketing.css:9004-9006 sets `.rf-marketing :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #91809f; outline-offset: 4px }`. The first has higher specificity (adds a type selector), so links/buttons/inputs get a blue 3px/5px ring while any other focusable element (e.g. `[tabindex]` — the OperationStory chapter heading at operation-story.tsx:265 has `tabIndex={-1}`, and the DemoForm success heading at demo-form.tsx:36) gets a mauve 3px/4px ring on the same page. `--ring: #7b49ab` is declared at marketing.css:39 and, verified by grep, `var(--ring)` appears zero times in the file. ux-spec §5 specifies "focus rings 2 px plum offset 2 px"; neither shipped rule matches in colour, width or offset.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Collapse to one `.rf-marketing :focus-visible` rule using `var(--ring)` at the spec's width/offset, and delete whichever of the two ported blocks is not wanted.

confirmedFindings.summary: The wordmark period is painted by an inline style, so it overrides both the `--primary` token and the later cascade rule that the port itself brought over.
confirmedFindings.detail: `BrandSignature` renders `<span className="brand-period" style={{ color: periodColor }}>` with `periodColor` defaulting to the literal `#10264d` (BrandMark.tsx:41, 58). An inline style beats any class selector, so both ported rules are dead on the marketing pages: `.rf-marketing .brand-period { color: var(--primary) }` (marketing.css:963) and — the one that actually wins in the source cascade — `.rf-marketing .brand-period, .rf-marketing .site-footer .brand-period { color: #8a8496 }` (marketing.css:8380). The header and footer brand therefore render a navy period where the ported design intends the grey `#8a8496`, on every marketing page. It also hard-codes a value that the token table (`--primary`, marketing.css:26) exists to own.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Drop the inline style and let `.brand-period` be painted by CSS (a `--brand-period-color` custom property the login page can override on its wrapper would keep the dark-panel escape hatch without defeating the cascade).

confirmedFindings.summary: `<Brand size={40}>` on the 404 page silently renders at 30px because `.rf-marketing .brand-mark` hard-codes the mark's box.
confirmedFindings.detail: not-found.tsx wraps itself in `.rf-marketing` and imports marketing.css, so the size prop that BrandMark writes onto the `<Image>` (width/height attributes) is overridden by CSS: `.rf-marketing .brand-mark { width:34px; height:34px }` (marketing.css:163) and then, later in the same cascade, `{ width:30px; height:30px }` (marketing.css:4401) — the last one wins for any mark without a more specific wrapper (`.passport-brand .brand-mark` 21px at 9701, `.mini-route-mark .brand-mark` 25px at 9722 are the only overrides). Verified by grepping every `.brand-mark` rule. The build-plan's P1 brief specifies "404: BrandMark 40 px + wordmark", and `.not-found-brand` — the class the page passes to hook this up (not-found.tsx:13) — has no rule anywhere in marketing.css (verified by a full className-vs-CSS scan).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `.rf-marketing .not-found-brand .brand-mark { width:40px; height:40px }`, or make BrandMark set the size via inline style/CSS variable so the prop is not silently inert inside the marketing scope.

confirmedFindings.summary: marketing.css is 9,776 lines against the ux-spec's ≤3,500-line consolidation target, and demonstrably retains dead and superseded declarations.
confirmedFindings.detail: `wc -l` reports 9,776 lines. ux-spec §1 asked for a consolidation that ports "the rules that actually paint" and drops "dead/duplicated declarations", targeting ≤3,500 lines; the file header instead states the nine source files were concatenated "in the redesign's own cascade order — later files intentionally restyle earlier ones". Concrete dead weight found while reviewing: `.rf-marketing .brand-mark` is declared at 163 (34px) and again at 4401 (30px) with the first fully superseded outside media queries; `.rf-marketing .brand-period` at 963 and 8380 are both dead because of the inline style in BrandSignature; `.faq-list [data-slot="accordion-item"]` (4998) matches no element in the ported FAQ markup; `--ring` (39) is referenced zero times; two conflicting global `:focus-visible` blocks (87, 9004) ship together. The oversize file is shipped on every marketing page and on `app/not-found.tsx`.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Do the consolidation pass the spec called for — collapse the duplicate `.brand-mark`/`.brand-period`/`:focus-visible` declarations to the winning value and delete selectors that match no ported markup — or record an explicit owner decision that the verbatim cascade is preferred and drop the line target from the spec.

confirmedFindings.summary: The 404 page renders with no marketing styles applied at all — at both desktop and mobile — so the ux-spec §3 404 anatomy (eyebrow chip, display H1, CTA button) fails in the browser.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Flow "404 /nope", viewports desktop (1440x900) and mobile (375x812). I opened both screenshots: C:/ClaudeCode/routeflow/.claude/worktrees/rf-watchdog/apps/web/test-output/artifacts/10-404-desktop.png and 10-404-mobile.png. Both show the page as raw browser default flow, flush against x=0 with no page padding, no centering, no type scale: the brand mark sits unsized top-left, the wordmark "routeflow." renders at body size, the eyebrow "404 · PAGE NOT FOUND" renders as plain body text with NO bullet dot (the `.eyebrow > span` dot that appears on every other marketing page is absent), the H1 "Let's get you / back on track." renders at body size, and the `className="button"` CTA "Back to RouteFlow →" renders as an unstyled inline link with no pill, no background, no padding. Every one of the classes used exists in the stylesheet — `.rf-marketing .not-found` (marketing.css:2465), `.rf-marketing .wrap` (:128), `.rf-marketing .eyebrow` (:247), `.rf-marketing .button` (:186) — and the wrapper div does carry `className="rf-marketing"` (not-found.tsx:11), so the selectors match; the stylesheet imported at not-found.tsx:3 is simply not reaching this route. Contrast with the same-run /privacy and /retailers screenshots, which are fully styled, proving the CSS itself is fine on `(marketing)` routes. The driver marked this flow "failed" but attributed the failure entirely to its own `.textContent()`/`
` assertion artifact and never inspected the styling, so this defect is unreported in the evidence. Caveat I can state precisely: this was observed against the driver's `next dev` server on localhost:3101; I did not run a production build, so whether `next build` also drops the CSS chunk for the root not-found segment is unverified.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Root not-found.tsx sits outside the `(marketing)` route group and is rendered by the root layout; its component-level `import "./(marketing)/marketing.css"` is not producing a stylesheet link on the 404 response. Decide the fix (e.g. move the import so the root layout emits it, or give the 404 its own route-group placement/layout) and re-observe /nope rendered in the browser at both viewports — reading source cannot prove it.

confirmedFindings.summary: The FAQ accordion is entirely unstyled: every question shows the browser's native disclosure triangle, the chevron icon wraps onto its own line below the question, item hairlines are missing, and the chevron never rotates on open.
confirmedFindings.detail: Flows "retailers /retailers" (desktop 1440x900 and mobile 375x812) and "home /" / "product /product" (mobile), which all render this shared component. Evidence: 05-retailers-faq-item3-desktop.png (I cropped y 2500-3400 at full width) and 05-retailers-faq-item3-mobile.png (y 3600-4100), plus 01-home-mobile.png (y 11640-11940) and 03-product-mobile.png. Every FAQ row renders as `▶ Who is RouteFlow for?` with the native `list-item` marker visible, and the lucide `ChevronDown` renders as a second, separate glyph on the line BELOW the question text, left-aligned under the marker, instead of right-aligned in the trigger row. On the item the driver opened ("Who handles my order or delivery questions?") the native marker flips to ▼ but the ChevronDown SVG stays pointing down — ux-spec §4 requires "chevron rotates on open". There are also no separators between items, because marketing.css:4998 styles `.rf-marketing .faq-list [data-slot="accordion-item"]` and no element in the markup carries that attribute — the component renders bare `<details>` elements (faq.tsx:78). Grepping the whole stylesheet for `summary`, `::marker`, `-webkit-details-marker` and `list-style` returns only `.rf-marketing summary:focus-visible` (marketing.css:91) and three unrelated `list-style:none` rules on `.check-list`, `.getting-started ol` and `.ai-review-steps` — nothing suppresses the marker or makes the trigger a flex row. `align-items: center` at marketing.css:1529 is a flex property applied to a non-flex `<summary>` and has no effect. The driver's assertions only checked `details.open` transitions, so it passed the flow and never looked at the rendering.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: The CSS was ported from the redesign's Radix Accordion (`[data-slot="accordion-trigger"]` / `accordion-item`) but the component was reimplemented on native `<details>/<summary>` (faq.tsx:78-88). Decide the trigger styling (suppress `::marker` and `::-webkit-details-marker`, make the summary a flex row with the chevron pushed right, add the item border, rotate the chevron on `[open]`, and either add `data-slot="accordion-item"` to the `<details>` or retarget marketing.css:4998), then re-observe an open and a closed item at both viewports.

confirmedFindings.summary: At 375px the /retailers hero H1 collapses into one run-on line with two missing word spaces: "Restock your shelves.Skip the backand forth."
confirmedFindings.detail:
Flow "retailers /retailers", mobile (375x812). Evidence: C:/ClaudeCode/routeflow/.claude/worktrees/rf-watchdog/apps/web/test-output/artifacts/05-retailers-faq-item3-mobile.png; I cropped y 60-380 at native resolution and read the headline as literally "Restock your shelves.Skip the backand forth." — no space after "shelves." and none between "back" and "and". The same page's desktop screenshot (05-retailers-faq-item3-desktop.png, crop y 0-700) renders correctly on three lines, so the defect is mobile-only. Two causes combine: (a) the JSX at retailers/page.tsx:53-58 places each text run on its own line immediately before a `
`, and JSX strips that trailing whitespace, so there is no literal space character between the runs; (b) `.rf-marketing .retailer-page .split-hero h1 br:last-of-type { display: none; }` (marketing.css:3979, inside `@media (max-width: 900px)`) hides BOTH `
` elements rather than the intended one, because `:last-of-type` is scoped per parent and the markup has one `
` directly under the `

` and a second under the ``. The driver independently confirmed this with computed styles (both `

confirmedFindings.fixHint:
Two decisions needed: whether to keep the responsive line-break suppression at all for this hero, and how to guarantee word spacing (explicit `{" "}` between runs, or a ``-per-line structure rather than `
`). If the rule is kept, `br:last-of-type` must be narrowed so it cannot match the ``'s own `

confirmedFindings.summary: The shared FAQ heading and the shared CTA heading lose their word spaces at mobile widths, rendering "Before youget started.", "Place your next orderwith a clearer view." and "Put your workflowto the test." across every marketing page.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Same defect class as the retailer hero but from two different CSS rules and two shared components, so it reaches nearly the whole site. Confirmed instances at 375x812 from native-resolution crops: (1) FAQ H2 "Before youget started." — 05-retailers-faq-item3-mobile.png y 3350-3650 and 01-home-mobile.png y ~11500 (also visible in 03-product-mobile.png); source faq.tsx:66-70, hidden by `.rf-marketing .faq-section h2 br { display: none; }` at marketing.css:2870 inside `@media (max-width: 760px)`. (2) Retailer CTA H2 "Place your next orderwith a clearer view." — 05-retailers-faq-item3-mobile.png y 4130-4450; source components/marketing.tsx:39-41. (3) Default CTA H2 "Put your workflowto the test." — 06-pricing-mobile.png y 3200-3900; source components/marketing.tsx:46-48. Both CTA variants are hidden by `.rf-marketing .cta-block br { display: none; }` at marketing.css:2665. In each case the JSX puts the text run on its own line before `
`, so JSX drops the whitespace and the words collide once the break is hidden. Because `FAQ` and `CTA` are shared components, this is visible on /, /product, /retailers, /wholesalers, /pricing and /company at mobile widths. Desktop is unaffected (05-retailers-faq-item3-desktop.png shows both headings correctly on two lines).
confirmedFindings.fixHint:
Decide the intended mobile layout for these headings (single wrapped line vs. keeping the break), then either insert explicit `{" "}` before each `
` in faq.tsx:66-70 and marketing.tsx:36-49, or drop the `display:none` rules at marketing.css:2665 and :2870. Re-observe /pricing, /retailers and / at 375px after the change — this must be judged rendered, not from source.

confirmedFindings.summary: Most below-the-fold sections were captured at opacity 0 in the full-page screenshots, so the requested design-system check is unjudgeable for the bulk of /, /product, /wholesalers, /pricing and /company.
confirmedFindings.detail: Reported as an evidence-sufficiency finding, per the instruction that insufficient evidence is itself a finding. I built a contact sheet of 01-home-mobile.png (375x13341, 8 vertical strips) and roughly half the page body is blank white: the problem grid, audience cards, buying-confidence block and CTA block are all absent, and the page jumps from the last FAQ item straight to the footer. The same blank region appears in 03-product-mobile.png (y 10000-10900) and 04-wholesalers-routes-tab-mobile.png (y 7250-8150). The cause is visible directly in 06-pricing-mobile.png at y 3200-3900, where the CTA block is captured MID-FADE — semi-transparent text over the panel — which matches `.rf-marketing .editorial-reveal.reveal-pending { opacity: 0 }` (marketing.css:9105) applied by editorial-motion.tsx:36 to every node below the fold at mount and only removed when the IntersectionObserver fires. Playwright's full-page capture does not scroll, so the observer never fires for those nodes. This is very likely a capture artifact rather than a user-facing defect — on /retailers, where the driver clicked FAQ items and forced a scroll, the CTA block and the sections around it did render (05-retailers-faq-item3-mobile.png) — but I cannot distinguish the two without driving the browser, which I am not permitted to do. Consequence either way: the requested design-system and a11y checks (invented colors/spacing, hover/focus/empty states, section fidelity against ux-spec §3) have NOT been performed for those sections at either viewport, and the driver's own assertions do not cover them because Playwright's `toBeVisible()` ignores opacity.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Re-drive these pages with the reveal state settled before capture (e.g. emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, which marketing.css:9123 forces to opacity 1, or scroll the page to the bottom before the full-page screenshot), then re-judge the below-fold sections. Do not change editorial-motion.tsx on the strength of this finding alone — first establish whether real users ever see the blank state.

Its premise "utilities have lower specificity than `.rf-marketing …` rules, so marketing pages keep their stylesheet's values" is false: the marketing typography rules match ANCESTORS, not the wordmark span, so they reach `.brand-wordmark` only by inheritance, and any declaration on the child beats an inherited value regardless of specificity. Evidence: (a) marketing.css:154-161 `.rf-marketing .brand { font-size:1.55rem; font-weight:650; letter-spacing:-0.065em }` is on the `<Link className="brand">` (site-header.tsx:43, site-footer.tsx:17), with responsive overrides at marketing.css:819 (1.35rem), :3108 (1.5rem), :5775 (1.4rem) — adding `text-[1.48rem]` to the wordmark would override all four; (b) the rule Fable cited near line 4396 is the header-scoped `.rf-marketing .brand { font-size:1.48rem; letter-spacing:-0.065em; gap:8px }` — also on the ancestor, and it carries NO font-weight (the 650 lives at :159 and is not `font-semibold`/600); (c) marketing.css:9692-9698 `.rf-marketing .passport-brand { font-size:12px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-0.045em }` wraps a bare `<BrandSignature />` at app/(marketing)/components/operation-story.tsx:276, so `text-[1.48rem]` would inflate that 12px passport wordmark to ~23.7px. All three break the stated invariant "Inside .rf-marketing the signature is pixel-identical to before". For the re-decision: the LAYOUT half of the design IS safe — `.rf-marketing .brand-signature` (marketing.css:9710-9714) is exactly `inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:9px`, so `inline-flex items-center gap-[9px]` utilities are value-identical everywhere; and apps/web/tailwind.config.ts:6-11 already contains `./components/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,mdx}` so no glob change is needed. remainingFindings.summary: The `signedIn` guard that keeps phones out of the marketing landing page reads presence cookies that only the Next web app writes — the mobile-web build never sets them — so every existing phone user of the mobile app now lands on the public marketing page at `/` instead of their app.
remainingFindings.detail:
State path: an operator uses RouteFlow on their phone at `https://www.routeflow.info`. Today (pre-diff) `skipMobileRedirect = optedOutOfMobile || /api/ || /_next/`, so EVERY phone request to `/` is rewritten to `MOBILE_WEB_URL/` and they land in the Expo mobile-web build, which does its own role routing. They sign in there; the middleware comment (middleware.ts:17-19) confirms the address bar stays on www.routeflow.info, so this is where these users live.

After the diff, middleware.ts:73-77 makes `/` exempt from the proxy unless `signedIn` (line 67) is true, and `signedIn` is read from `rf-op-auth` / `rf-buyer-auth`. Evidence those cookies cannot exist for a mobile-web user: `apps/web/lib/presence-cookies.ts:26-50` sets them with `document.cookie` from inside the Next web app only (callers: `apps/web/lib/auth.ts:7`, `apps/web/lib/buyer-auth.ts:95`); a grep for `rf-op-auth|rf-buyer-auth|OP_PRESENCE_COOKIE|BUYER_PRESENCE_COOKIE` and for `document.cookie` across `apps/mobile/**/*.ts(x)` returns ZERO hits. The Expo build keeps its session in its own storage.

So for the entire existing mobile population `signedIn === false` and `/` is exempt. Concretely: a signed-in mobile-web operator opens their bookmark `https://www.routeflow.info/` → no presence cookie → line 77 is true → no rewrite → `resolveLandingTarget` returns null → they are served the desktop marketing landing page with 'Book a demo', not their app. The escape route makes it worse, not better: tapping 'Sign in → Distributor' goes to `/login`, which is NOT in MARKETING_PATHS, so it IS proxied — they bounce into the mobile app's login screen despite already being signed in there.

The new test file pins exactly this behaviour as correct: `does not proxy / for a signed-out phone (R-MKT T11)` passes (I ran `npx jest --runInBand middleware.marketing` in apps/web: 25/25 pass). Nothing in the suite models a phone whose session lives in the mobile-web build, because that session is invisible to the middleware by construction.

This is the opposite failure from the already-known '/ redirect fires on phones and sends them to /dashboard' item: the implementation's `signedIn` clause does prevent that, but the signal it depends on is unobtainable for the users it was written to protect, so the clause is effectively dead for them. (It can only ever fire for a phone that signed in through the desktop UI after `?desktop=1` AND whose 30-day `prefer-desktop` cookie has since lapsed while the sliding presence cookie stayed fresh.)
remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide the intended contract for `/` on a phone. Options: (a) keep proxying `/` for phones unconditionally (drop `/` from the carve-out) and reach the marketing home on phones via an explicit path/`?desktop=1`; (b) have the mobile-web build set the presence cookie on sign-in so the middleware can see it; (c) serve the marketing landing at `/` on phones but give the mobile-web build a visible re-entry link. Any choice needs a middleware test that models a phone with NO presence cookie but an active mobile-web session.
remainingFindings.decision: The presence cookies are written only by the Next web app's document.cookie callers, so a mobile-web user who was signed in inside the Expo build carries no rf-op-auth/rf-buyer-auth and, with `/` now exempt from the proxy, is served the marketing landing instead of their app on every visit to the root. This is the complement of the already-raised 'signed-in phone redirect' finding (cookies present) and is not covered by it; it is an undecided behavior change for every existing phone user's entry path, not a deliberate product ruling.

The marketing pages are now, for the first time, rendered on phones — and the `<head>` the root layout emits (apps/web/app/layout.tsx) asks the same origin for: `/brand/routeflow-mark-64.png` (icons.icon + shortcut, layout.tsx:85,87), `/brand/routeflow-mark-180.png` (icons.apple, :86), `/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png` (appleWebApp.startupImage, :82), `/operator-manifest.json` (manifest, :77) and `/brand/routeflow-mark-512.png` (openGraph.images, :94). `ServiceWorkerRegistry` (layout.tsx:110, components/ServiceWorkerRegistry.tsx:7) additionally requests `/sw.js`. None of these six paths is in MARKETING_PATHS and none matches the matcher's exclusions, so on a phone each is proxied to the Expo Railway origin, which does not serve them.

Observable failures for a phone visitor on /, /product, /pricing, …: no apple-touch-icon; the manifest response is the Expo build's HTML, so Chrome logs `Manifest: Line: 1, column: 1, Syntax error` and 'Add to Home Screen' is unavailable from the new marketing site; `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js')` rejects on an unsupported MIME type (swallowed by the .catch, so it is a console error only); and Googlebot-Smartphone (UA contains both `Android` and `Mobile`, so `isMobileUserAgent` matches) cannot fetch the og:image it is told about.

Why every earlier lens missed it: the unit suite only iterates `MARKETING_PAGE_PATHS` plus the two metadata routes; the UI-verify `console-errors` / `network-failures` flows ran a desktop browser resized to 375px, which sends a DESKTOP user agent, so the proxy never engaged; Playwright T12 asserts only the /pricing HTML body. Note this is NOT the known '/unmatched marketing path never reaches the 404' item — that is about page routes; this is about the subresources a successfully-served marketing page then requests. The visible marks are fine, because BrandMark goes through `next/image` → `/_next/image?...`, which the matcher does exclude.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Extend the proxy skip beyond exact page paths — e.g. also skip `/brand/`, `/marketing/`, `/sw.js` and the two manifest JSONs, or (cleaner) exclude static asset paths in the middleware `matcher` itself the way `_next/static` already is. Add a middleware test row asserting `/brand/routeflow-mark-64.png` and `/operator-manifest.json` are NOT rewritten for a mobile UA.
remainingFindings.decision: The exemption is exact-match over page paths plus robots/sitemap while the matcher excludes only _next/static, _next/image and favicon.ico, and the passing T11 pin proves any other path with a phone UA is rewritten to the mobile-web origin — so the root layout's /brand/*.png icons, apple-touch icon, manifest and OG image requested by a phone rendering the marketing HTML are fetched from the wrong origin. Pre-diff this was invisible because the whole phone session was proxied consistently; now the page and its head assets split origins.

remainingFindings.summary: This diff introduces `next/image` into apps/web for the first time (and puts it on the login, signup, all buyer auth, platform-admin and two money-preview surfaces), but apps/web declares no `sharp` dependency and the web runner image is a bare standalone bundle — if sharp is not traced in, `/_next/image` 500s and the brand mark vanishes app-wide.
remainingFindings.detail:
Evidence gathered this session: (1) `grep -rln "from \"next/image\"" apps/web/app apps/web/components packages/ui/src` excluding `(marketing)` returns exactly one file — `apps/web/components/brand/BrandMark.tsx:1`. Inside `(marketing)` it returns company/page.tsx, components/operation-story.tsx, components/technology-art.tsx. So before this diff apps/web used `next/image` nowhere; after it, every BrandMark render on `(auth)/login`, `(auth)/signup`, the eight `buyer/*` pages, `(platform-admin)/layout.tsx`, `(dashboard)/customers/[id]` statement preview and `(dashboard)/bookkeeping/[transactionId]` invoice preview goes through the image optimizer. (2) `grep '"sharp"' apps/web/package.json` → no match; in package-lock.json the only owner of `node_modules/sharp` (0.35.4) is `apps/api`. (3) `apps/web/Dockerfile` builder copies root manifests + `packages/*` + `apps/web/package.json` only — `apps/api/package.json` is never copied — then `npm ci`; the runner stage is `node:20-alpine` with only `.next/standalone`, `.next/static` and `public` copied in. (4) `next.config.mjs` sets `output: "standalone"` and does NOT set `images: { unoptimized: true }`. Next is pinned at 14.2.35 (apps/web/package.json:44).

Failure scenario if sharp is not resolvable in the deployed standalone server: every `/_next/image?url=%2Fbrand%2Froutefow-mark-192.png…` request answers 500, so the shared mark is a broken image on every authenticated and auth-entry surface the port just converted to it, and the marketing photography fails too — i.e. the visible half of R4/R12 is dead on deploy day while every Jest/tsc/eslint gate stays green (RTL never renders the optimizer).

HONEST LIMIT: I did NOT verify the outcome. Proving it needs a `docker build -f apps/web/Dockerfile` and an inspection of `.next/standalone/node_modules/sharp`, which I did not run. What I verified is the exposure: a first-time `next/image` dependency in a standalone image whose workspace does not declare sharp and whose only lockfile owner of sharp is a workspace the web build does not even copy the manifest for. The musl binary (`@img/sharp-linuxmusl-x64`) IS in the lockfile and apps/api runs alpine, so sharp is installable — the open question is purely whether it is present and traced into the web standalone output.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either add `sharp` to apps/web's dependencies (belt-and-braces for standalone, as Next documents), or prove with one Docker build that `.next/standalone/**/sharp` exists and `/_next/image` returns 200 for `/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png` before this ships. If neither is acceptable, drop back to plain `` for BrandMark (it is a fixed-size square PNG, so optimization buys little) and keep `next/image` only where R12 requires it.
remainingFindings.decision: apps/web declares no sharp, package-lock puts it only under apps/api, and the web runner is a standalone bundle — exactly the configuration in which Next 14 refuses /_next/image at request time ('sharp is required to be installed in standalone mode'), which would blank the BrandMark on login, signup, every buyer auth page, platform-admin and the two money previews. The evidence does not show images.unoptimized or an `unoptimized` prop that would neutralise it, and the visual checks ran against dev, not the Docker image, so the candidate stays; it is the one item that must be proved against the production image before merge.

remainingFindings.summary: Three of the four auth CTAs the new marketing chrome ships (/signup, /buyer/login, /buyer/register) are not in the mobile-proxy exemption set, so on a phone they are rewritten to the Expo mobile-web build, which has no such routes — the visitor is silently dumped on the Expo app's own landing screen and never reaches a sign-up or retailer sign-in form.
remainingFindings.detail:
State path, verified end to end in this session:

(1) The exemption set is exactly `MARKETING_PAGE_PATHS` + two metadata routes. `apps/web/lib/marketing-routes.ts:19-30` lists `/`, `/product`, `/wholesalers`, `/retailers`, `/pricing`, `/company`, `/contact`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/distributors`. `middleware.ts:29-33` spreads that plus `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`. `/login`, `/signup`, `/buyer/login`, `/buyer/register` are NOT members, so `middleware.ts:77` leaves `skipMobileRedirect` false and `middleware.ts:79-88` rewrites to `https://routeflowmobile-production.up.railway.app<pathname>`.

(2) The new chrome links all four on every page. `app/(marketing)/components/auth-links.ts:7-10` = `/login`, `/signup`, `/buyer/login`, `/buyer/register`. `site-footer.tsx:42-50` renders all four in the 'Your workspace' column of the footer, i.e. on all 9 public pages. `site-header.tsx:80-93` (sign-in dropdown) and `:140-147` (mobile sheet) render `/login` + `/buyer/login`. `retailers/page.tsx:64` is the page's primary green CTA -> `authLinks.retailerSignUp` (`/buyer/register`), `:71` -> `/buyer/login`.

(3) The Expo build has none of those routes. `find apps/mobile/app -maxdepth 2 -type d` returns only `(auth)`, `(customer)`, `(driver)`, `(operator)`, `(tenant)`; `ls apps/mobile/app/(auth)` shows `login.tsx` but no `signup`; there is no `buyer` segment anywhere in the tree, and `find apps/mobile/app -name '+not-found*'` returns nothing.

(4) The mobile service answers 200 for any path: `apps/mobile/Dockerfile` nginx block `location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; }`.

(5) What the visitor then sees: expo-router registers its built-in `Unmatched` screen for `NOT_FOUND_ROUTE_NAME` (`apps/mobile/node_modules/expo-router/build/ExpoRoot.js:153`; `constants.js:5` -> `'+not-found'`; `views/Unmatched.js:54-56` renders an h1 'Unmatched Route'). Then `apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:88-104` fires: for a signed-out visitor, `segments[0]` is `'+not-found'`, which is neither `(auth)` nor `(customer)`/`(operator)`/`(driver)`, so it hits the else branch `router.replace("/")` and the browser lands on the Expo app's static landing screen (`apps/mobile/app/index.tsx`, a marketing screen, not a router).

Concrete failure: a retailer on an iPhone opens www.routeflow.info/retailers, taps the page's main green 'Create retailer account' button -> the URL becomes /buyer/register, the Expo SPA boots, flashes 'Unmatched Route', then client-side replaces the URL with '/' and shows the Expo mobile landing page. The registration form is unreachable on a phone. Same for footer 'Create distributor account' (/signup) and 'Retailer sign in' (/buyer/login) on all 9 pages. Only /login survives (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx exists, and `_layout.tsx:88` skips the replace because `segments[0] === "(auth)"`).

Why nothing caught it: T3 (`e2e/36-marketing-site.spec.ts:246-290`) crawls the links with the `marketing` project's context, which `playwright.config.ts:565-568` pins to `devices["Desktop Chrome"]` — desktop UA, so the Next pages answer normally. Even a UA-swapped rerun would pass, because the nginx fallback returns 200 for every one of these paths; the assertion is on `status < 400`, not on content. This directly contradicts R3 ('Every internal link resolves on the live app') for the population R11 was written to serve.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide the contract for phones: either add the four auth paths to the mobile-proxy exemption (so phones get the Next auth pages, matching the desktop marketing site they came from), or point the marketing chrome's auth links at the mobile-web equivalents when the visitor is on a phone. Then add a mobile-UA content assertion (not a status assertion) to T3.
remainingFindings.decision: The evidence traces the full path: the exemption set is exactly MARKETING_PAGE_PATHS plus two metadata routes, the new chrome links /signup, /buyer/login and /buyer/register from every page's footer and header, and a phone UA on those paths is rewritten to the Expo mobile-web origin which has no such routes. Rendering the marketing site on phones for the first time turns its primary conversion CTAs into dead ends, a regression the port itself creates; /login still reaches an Expo login screen, so major rather than blocker.

remainingFindings.summary: The `!(pathname === "/" && signedIn)` guard that is supposed to preserve the pre-port landing behaviour for signed-in phones can never fire, because the Expo mobile-web build never writes the presence cookies it reads — so returning mobile-web users lose their 'type the domain, land in my app' entry point.
remainingFindings.detail:
`middleware.ts:70-77` computes `signedIn` from `OP_PRESENCE_COOKIE` / `BUYER_PRESENCE_COOKIE` and uses it to keep the pre-port proxy for a signed-in phone at '/'. The comment at `middleware.ts:64-69` and again at `:89-96` states 'a signed-in phone at "/" was already proxied to the mobile-web build and never reaches this block'.

That is false in production. The presence cookies are written only by `apps/web/lib/presence-cookies.ts:27-29` via `document.cookie`, from the Next.js web app's auth code. `grep -rni cookie` over `apps/mobile/{app,lib,hooks,store,utils,components}` (ts/tsx, node_modules excluded) returns ZERO hits — the Expo build stores its session in AsyncStorage/SecureStore and never touches `document.cookie`. So for every mobile-web user `signedIn === false`, `isMarketingPath("/")` is true, and '/' is exempted from the proxy.

What changes for them: `apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:71-80` routes a signed-in buyer at '/' to `/(customer)/(tabs)/home`, and `:167-172` routes a signed-in operator at '/' to `/(operator)/home`. So before this change, a returning mobile-web user who opened www.routeflow.info was auto-routed into their app. After it, they get the desktop marketing homepage instead, and their only way back is to tap a control labelled 'Sign in' (`/login`, which does proxy through and, via `_layout.tsx:167`, lands them in the app) — while the two retailer controls are the dead ends of the finding above.

Second consequence: the test block 'middleware landing carve-out, signed in' in `apps/web/app/(marketing)/middleware.marketing.test.ts` manufactures `rf-op-auth=1` / `rf-buyer-auth=1` on an iPhone request. Those two rows are green and vacuous — they pin a state the mobile build cannot produce, so they give false assurance that the pre-port landing behaviour is preserved for phones.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either accept and document that mobile-web users now see the marketing homepage (and drop or re-scope the dead `signedIn` clause plus its two vacuous test rows), or give the mobile-web build a way to advertise its session to the middleware (it runs on the same www.routeflow.info origin for the document, so a presence cookie written by the Expo web bootstrap would work).
remainingFindings.decision: The presence cookies are written only by apps/web's presence-cookies.ts and a grep of the Expo app shows it never touches document.cookie, so signedIn is always false for a mobile-web user and the guard plus its two comments describe behaviour that cannot occur. The user-facing cost is one extra tap (Sign in → /login → Expo), but the code carries a false correctness claim and dead logic that will mislead the next editor.

remainingFindings.summary: Every marketing page now renders on phones declaring a manifest, favicon, apple-touch-icon and OG image under /brand and /operator-manifest.json — none of which are in the mobile-proxy exemption, so a phone gets the Expo SPA's index.html (200, text/html) for all of them.
remainingFindings.detail:
The middleware matcher is `["/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)"]` (`middleware.ts:226`) — it excludes only `_next/static`, `_next/image` and `/favicon.ico`. `/brand/*` and `/operator-manifest.json` therefore reach the middleware, are not members of `MARKETING_PATHS` (`middleware.ts:29-33`), and under a mobile UA are rewritten to the mobile-web origin, where nginx's `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html` (`apps/mobile/Dockerfile`) returns the Expo SPA HTML with a 200.

The root layout now points every one of these at those paths: `app/layout.tsx:77` `manifest: "/operator-manifest.json"`, `:82` `startupImage: "/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png"`, `:85` `icon: /brand/routeflow-mark-64.png`, `:86` `apple: /brand/routeflow-mark-180.png`, `:87` `shortcut: /brand/routeflow-mark-64.png`, `:94` `openGraph.images: /brand/routeflow-mark-512.png`.

This is new because before the port a phone never rendered any of this HTML — every public path was proxied at the door. Concrete failures on an iPhone at www.routeflow.info/pricing: the `<link rel="manifest">` fetch returns HTML, so the manifest fails to parse and 'Add to Home Screen' has no name/icons/start_url; the apple-touch-icon fetch returns HTML, so the home-screen icon falls back to a screenshot; the tab/favicon fetch returns HTML. Googlebot-Smartphone (UA contains both 'Android' and 'Mobile', so `isMobileUserAgent` at `middleware.ts:36-42` matches it — the new test file's own comment says so) gets HTML for the og:image URL.

Not affected, and worth noting so the fix is scoped correctly: `BrandMark` and the three marketing photos go through `next/image`, whose browser request is `/_next/image?url=...`, and `_next/image` IS excluded by the matcher, so those render.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add the static asset prefixes the public pages reference (`/brand/`, `/marketing/`) and the two manifest JSON files to the mobile-proxy skip list, or exclude them in the middleware matcher alongside `_next/static`.
remainingFindings.decision: The matcher excludes only _next/static, _next/image and /favicon.ico, /brand/* and /operator-manifest.json are not in MARKETING_PATHS, and nginx's try_files on the mobile-web origin answers 200 text/html for unknown paths — so every phone visitor to the marketing site gets SPA HTML for the manifest, icons, apple-touch-icon and startup image the new root layout declares. This is new exposure because before the port a phone never rendered a Next page that referenced these assets.

remainingFindings.summary: This change introduces the app's first-ever use of next/image while apps/web has no `images` config (so optimization is on) and `output: "standalone"` — a combination in which Next 14.2.35 hard-throws a 500 if `sharp` is missing, and `sharp` is not a dependency of the web workspace nor of the web Docker build's manifest set.
remainingFindings.detail:
Verified facts:

- `apps/web/next.config.mjs` has NO `images` key at all — no `unoptimized: true`, no loader override — so `<Image>` uses the default loader and the browser requests `/_next/image?url=...`. Line 9 of that file sets `output: "standalone"`.
- `node_modules/next/dist/server/image-optimizer.js:664-668`: in `optimizeImage`, when `sharp` is falsy AND `nextConfigOutput === "standalone"`, Next logs `'sharp' is required to be installed in standalone mode...` and `throw new ImageError(500, "Internal Server Error")`. The squoosh fallback below it is unreachable in standalone. `sharp` is loaded at `:155-157` via `require(process.env.NEXT_SHARP_PATH || "sharp")` inside a try/catch, so a missing module leaves it undefined silently.
- `sharp` is not in `apps/web/package.json`. The only manifest declaring it is `apps/api/package.json:84`.
- `apps/web/Dockerfile` builder copies root `package.json`/`package-lock.json`/`turbo.json`, the `packages/*` manifests, and `apps/web/package.json` — it never copies `apps/api/package.json` (contrast `apps/api/Dockerfile:27`, which copies its own). So apps/api is not an on-disk workspace in the web image.
- `git grep next/image HEAD -- apps/web` returns only a middleware matcher string and two eslint-disable comments — no component ever imported `next/image` before this change. There is therefore zero production evidence that `/_next/image` works in the deployed web image.

NOT verified, and I am saying so explicitly: I could not confirm whether root `npm ci` still materialises `node_modules/sharp` from the lockfile when apps/api is absent, nor whether @vercel/nft traces the dynamic `require(process.env.NEXT_SHARP_PATH || "sharp")` into `.next/standalone`. `next build` was never run in this worktree (only a dev `.next`; `apps/web/.next/standalone` does not exist), and I did not build the image. `node_modules/next/dist/build/collect-build-traces.js:250-254` only *ignores* sharp under `hasNextSupport` (Vercel), so it is not deliberately excluded — but nothing in the repo pins it in either.

Failure scenario if sharp is absent from the runner: every `/_next/image` request returns 500. `BrandMark` renders nothing on the operator login page, signup, buyer login/register/invite/change-password/forgot/reset/verify, the buyer-portal sidebar, the customer statement preview, the bookkeeping invoice preview and the platform-admin sidebar; and the three `next/image` photos (`(marketing)/company/page.tsx:2`, `components/operation-story.tsx:4`, `components/technology-art.tsx:1`) fail on the marketing pages. Because `alt=""` on the mark, it degrades to blank space rather than a broken-image glyph — silent on every surface.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Pin it rather than leave it to tracing luck: either add `sharp` to apps/web's dependencies (and confirm the alpine musl binaries land, as apps/api already does), or set `images: { unoptimized: true }` in next.config.mjs since every image here is a local static asset. Whichever is chosen, prove it against a built image before merge — this is the first next/image in the app.
remainingFindings.decision: The quoted image-optimizer.js lines show Next 14.2 hard-throws a 500 when sharp is absent under output: "standalone" in production, next.config.mjs has no images config so optimization is on, and sharp is declared only by apps/api. Whether hoisting plus standalone tracing happens to carry apps/api's sharp into the web runner image is not settled by the truncated Dockerfile evidence, so this is kept: if it does not, every BrandMark on every page is a 500 in prod and the fix (unoptimized) is one line.

remainingFindings.summary: The port adds a second copy of the Geist typeface to git (141 KB of woff2 under apps/web/fonts/) while an unreferenced 134 KB woff copy of the same family already sits tracked at apps/web/app/fonts/, and the spec's residual row naming the heavy-files exemption omits the new fonts directory.
remainingFindings.detail:
`apps/web/app/fonts.ts:8,16` points `next/font/local` at `../fonts/Geist-Variable.woff2` and `../fonts/GeistMono-Variable.woff2` — new untracked binaries (69,652 B and 71,368 B, `ls -la apps/web/fonts`).

`git ls-files apps/web/app/fonts` shows `app/fonts/GeistVF.woff` and `app/fonts/GeistMonoVF.woff` are already tracked (66,268 B + 67,864 B, dated 2026-09-04, i.e. pre-existing on HEAD). `grep -rn "GeistVF\|GeistMonoVF"` across apps/web (ts/tsx/css/js, node_modules and .next excluded) returns nothing — they are referenced by no code, no CSS and no config. So the repo now carries the same typeface family twice, ~275 KB total, one copy dead.

This matters under two of the project's own rules: CLAUDE.md's heavy-files policy ('No images, videos, or office binaries in git', with the repo going public for CI and clones expected to stay lean), and R15 'Dead weight is not ported'. Separately, `spec.md:45`'s residual row says the CLAUDE.md amendment should name `public/brand` + `public/marketing` as required build assets — it does not name `apps/web/fonts/`, which is equally a new tracked binary directory and will trip the same policy on the next audit.

Note: the dead `app/fonts/*.woff` pair predates this change; the defect this change contributes is the duplicate plus the incomplete residual.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Delete the unreferenced apps/web/app/fonts/GeistVF.woff and GeistMonoVF.woff, and add apps/web/fonts/ to the spec's CLAUDE.md heavy-files residual alongside public/brand and public/marketing.
remainingFindings.decision: The port adds 141 KB of Geist woff2 while a 134 KB tracked woff copy of the same family sits unreferenced under app/fonts/, so the repo carries the family twice against R15's dead-weight rule and the heavy-files policy, and the spec's residual row does not name the new directory. The stale copy predates the port, but the port was the moment to replace rather than duplicate it.
